attributes.description: Typical range of metal grades observed in this geological unit (e.g., 0.5-1.2% Cu, 55-62% Fe). Provides context for grade control and cut-off grade decisions. Nullable for non-ore units.

attributes.name: unit_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the geological unit across all mine sites. Used consistently in drillhole logging, block model coding, and grade control. Sourced from Geovia GEMS formation tables.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Geovia GEMS Data Dictionary

attributes.name: unit_name
attributes.description: Full formal name of the geological unit (e.g., lithological formation, stratigraphic member, intrusive phase, alteration assemblage, weathering horizon). Human-readable identifier used in geological reports and cross-section interpretation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, International Stratigraphic Guide

attributes.name: unit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the geological unit by its primary geological nature: lithological (rock type), stratigraphic (formation/member), structural (fault/fold zone), alteration (hydrothermal/metamorphic assemblage), weathering (oxidation/supergene horizon), or intrusive (igneous phase).
attributes.references: International Stratigraphic Guide, JORC Code 2012 Edition

attributes.name: weathering_state
attributes.description: Degree of weathering or oxidation of the geological unit. Influences geotechnical properties, ore recovery rates, and processing methods (oxide vs. sulphide ore).
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, ISRM Rock Mass Classification

products.name: production_drillhole
products.description: Master register of all drillholes (exploration, resource definition, grade control, geotechnical, and hydrogeological) across all projects and mine sites. Records collar location (easting, northing, RL), azimuth, dip, total depth, hole type (RC, diamond, RAB, AC), drilling contractor, rig identifier, purpose, status, and JORC reporting category. The SSOT for drillhole identity — geology domain owns the master record; exploration domain references via FK for program planning. Integrates with Geovia GEMS and LabWare LIMS for assay linkage.
products.reference: JORC Code 2012 – Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: production_drillhole_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the production drillhole record. Primary key for the production drillhole master register.

attributes.name: capital_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the mining project or tenement under which this drillhole was executed.

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Grade control drilling is a direct mining operational cost allocated to cost centres for unit cost calculation and AISC reporting. Mining operations track drilling costs per cost centre for budget var

attributes.name: drill_hole_id
attributes.description: Business identifier for the drillhole, typically a site-specific alphanumeric code used in geological logs, assay reports, and JORC disclosures. This is the externally-known unique code for the hole.

attributes.name: drill_program_id
attributes.description: Reference to the exploration or grade control drill program under which this hole was planned and executed.

attributes.name: drill_rig_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to equipment.asset. Business justification: Production drillholes must reference the specific drill rig asset for equipment utilization tracking, maintenance correlation with hole quality metrics, and operational planning. Replaces unlinked rig

attributes.name: geologist_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Grade control and production drilling require tracking which geologist logged the hole for accountability, QAQC audits, competency verification, and JORC compliance. Real-world mining operations link

attributes.name: laboratory_sample_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.laboratory_sample. Business justification: Production drillholes generate samples sent to laboratory for grade control assay. Links drilling location and depth to laboratory analysis for spatial grade distribution and mining reconciliation. Es

attributes.name: orebody_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.orebody. Business justification: Production drillholes target specific orebodies for grade control and resource definition. Currently production_drillhole has site_id but no orebody_id. Adding orebody_id FK enables direct linkage of

attributes.name: site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the mine site where the drillhole is located.

attributes.name: azimuth
attributes.description: Planned azimuth (bearing) of the drillhole at collar, measured in degrees from 0 to 360, where 0/360 is north, 90 is east, 180 is south, and 270 is west. Used to define hole trajectory.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, Drilling Standards

attributes.name: collar_easting
attributes.description: Easting coordinate of the drillhole collar (surface location) in the site coordinate reference system, typically in meters. Used for spatial positioning in GIS and geological modeling systems.
attributes.references: GIS Coordinate Standard, JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1

attributes.name: collar_northing
attributes.description: Northing coordinate of the drillhole collar (surface location) in the site coordinate reference system, typically in meters. Used for spatial positioning in GIS and geological modeling systems.
attributes.references: GIS Coordinate Standard, JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1

attributes.name: collar_rl
attributes.description: Reduced Level (elevation) of the drillhole collar relative to site datum, typically in meters above mean sea level. Critical for accurate 3D geological modeling and resource estimation.
attributes.references: Site Survey Standard, JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for recording operational notes, drilling issues, geological observations, or other relevant information about the drillhole. Used for quality control and historical reference.

attributes.name: completion_date
attributes.description: Date when drilling operations were completed or abandoned. Used for program scheduling, performance tracking, and cost allocation.

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: Coordinate reference system (CRS) or projection used for collar coordinates. Examples: MGA94 Zone 50, WGS84 UTM Zone 51S, local mine grid. Critical for spatial data integration.
attributes.references: GIS Standard, JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1

attributes.name: core_diameter_mm
attributes.description: Diameter of the drill core or bit size in millimeters. Common sizes include HQ (63.5mm), NQ (47.6mm), PQ (85mm) for diamond drilling, or bit diameter for RC/RAB drilling.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, Drilling Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this drillhole record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: datum
attributes.description: Vertical datum used for collar RL (elevation). Examples: AHD (Australian Height Datum), MSL (Mean Sea Level), site-specific datum. Critical for accurate 3D modeling.
attributes.references: Survey Standard, JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1

attributes.name: dip
attributes.description: Planned dip (inclination) of the drillhole at collar, measured in degrees from -90 (vertically down) to +90 (vertically up). Negative values indicate downward drilling. Used to define hole trajectory.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, Drilling Standards

attributes.name: driller_name
attributes.description: Name of the lead driller or drilling supervisor responsible for executing the drillhole. Used for quality control and performance tracking.

attributes.name: drilling_contractor
attributes.description: Name of the drilling contractor company that executed the drillhole. Used for quality control, performance tracking, and contractor management.

attributes.name: hole_purpose
attributes.description: Primary purpose of the drillhole: Exploration (greenfield discovery), Resource Definition (resource estimation), Grade Control (short-term mine planning), Geotechnical (rock mechanics), Hydrogeological (water management), or Condemnation (infrastructure siting).

attributes.name: hole_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the drillhole: Planned (scheduled but not started), In Progress (drilling underway), Completed (drilling finished), Abandoned (terminated early), Suspended (paused), Logged (geological logging complete), Assayed (laboratory results received). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Planned|In Progress|Completed|Abandoned|Suspended|Logged|Assayed — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: hole_type
attributes.description: Type of drilling method used: RC (Reverse Circulation), Diamond (core drilling), RAB (Rotary Air Blast), AC (Air Core), Rotary, or Percussion.

attributes.name: is_assayed
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether samples from this drillhole have been submitted to the laboratory and assay results received. True if assayed, False if not yet assayed.

attributes.name: is_surveyed
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether downhole survey measurements have been completed to determine actual hole trajectory. True if surveyed, False if not yet surveyed.

attributes.name: jorc_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Joint Ore Reserves Committee (JORC) Resource Category
attributes.description: JORC resource classification category that this drillhole contributes to: Measured (highest confidence), Indicated (moderate confidence), Inferred (lowest confidence), Exploration (pre-resource), or Non-JORC (not used in resource estimation).

attributes.name: logged_date
attributes.description: Date when geological logging of the drillhole was completed. Represents when lithological, structural, and mineralisation observations were recorded.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this drillhole record was last modified. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and change tracking.

attributes.name: planned_depth
attributes.description: Originally planned depth for the drillhole in meters. Used to compare against actual total depth for program performance tracking.

attributes.name: recovery_percent
attributes.description: Average core recovery percentage for the drillhole, calculated as (recovered core length / drilled length) × 100. Critical quality indicator for diamond drilling and resource confidence classification.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, Drilling Standards

attributes.name: sample_interval_m
attributes.description: Standard sampling interval length in meters used for this drillhole. Typical intervals are 1m for grade control, 2m for resource drilling, or variable for geological contacts.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, Sampling Standards

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Date when drilling operations commenced for this hole. Used for program scheduling and performance tracking.

attributes.name: survey_method
attributes.description: Method used to survey the drillhole trajectory (azimuth and dip at depth intervals). Common methods include Gyroscopic, Magnetic, Electronic Multi-Shot, Single Shot, Optical, or Downhole Camera.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, Survey Standards

attributes.name: total_depth
attributes.description: Total depth drilled from collar, measured in meters along the hole trajectory. Represents the final depth achieved before completion or abandonment.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, Drilling Standards

products.name: production_drillhole_survey
products.description: Downhole directional survey records for each drillhole capturing depth, azimuth, and dip measurements at regular intervals to define the actual 3D trajectory of the hole. Essential for accurate spatial positioning of all downhole data (assays, lithology, geotechnics) and for de-surveying collar coordinates into 3D space. Sourced from gyroscopic and magnetic survey instruments logged into Geovia GEMS.

attributes.name: production_drillhole_survey_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the drillhole survey record. Primary key for the production drillhole survey entity.

attributes.name: drill_hole_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the parent drillhole for which this survey record was captured. Links this survey measurement to the specific drillhole being surveyed.

attributes.name: production_drillhole_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.production_drillhole. Business justification: production_drillhole_survey records directional survey measurements for a specific production drillhole. Currently only links to exploration.drill_hole, but the survey belongs to the production_drillh

attributes.name: survey_run_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the survey run or batch in which this measurement was captured. Multiple survey points may be captured in a single survey run down the hole.

attributes.name: surveyor_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Downhole survey quality and QAQC require tracking surveyor identity for competency verification, audit trails, and accountability. Survey accuracy directly impacts resource estimation and mine design,

attributes.name: azimuth_degrees
attributes.description: Horizontal direction of the drillhole at this survey point, measured in degrees clockwise from true north (0-360). Used to calculate the 3D trajectory of the hole.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for surveyor notes, observations, or explanations regarding this survey measurement. May include information about survey conditions, instrument issues, or data quality concerns.

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: Name or code of the coordinate reference system (CRS) used for the calculated spatial coordinates (e.g., MGA94 Zone 50, WGS84 UTM Zone 31N). Critical for spatial data integration and GIS compatibility.

attributes.name: correction_applied_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether magnetic declination, temperature, or other correction factors have been applied to the raw survey measurements. True indicates corrected data, false indicates raw uncorrected data.

attributes.name: correction_factor
attributes.description: Numerical correction factor applied to the raw survey measurements to account for magnetic declination, instrument drift, or environmental interference. Null if no correction was applied.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this survey record was first created in the Geovia GEMS system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: depth_metres
attributes.description: Measured depth down the drillhole from the collar at which this survey reading was taken, expressed in metres. Critical for spatial positioning of all downhole data.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Drilling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: dip_degrees
attributes.description: Vertical inclination of the drillhole at this survey point, measured in degrees from horizontal. Negative values indicate downward inclination, positive values indicate upward inclination. Typically ranges from -90 (vertical down) to +90 (vertical up).

attributes.name: easting_coordinate
attributes.description: Calculated easting (X) coordinate of this survey point in the mine coordinate system, derived from collar position and survey trajectory. Used for 3D spatial positioning in GIS and block models.

attributes.name: elevation_rl
attributes.description: Calculated elevation (Z) coordinate of this survey point relative to a defined datum, expressed as Reduced Level (RL) in metres. Used for 3D spatial positioning in GIS and block models.

attributes.name: gravity_field_strength
attributes.description: Measured gravitational field strength at this survey point, expressed in g-units. Used by gyroscopic instruments for orientation reference.

attributes.name: magnetic_dip_angle
attributes.description: Angle of the local magnetic field relative to horizontal, measured in degrees. Used for magnetic survey correction and quality validation.

attributes.name: magnetic_field_strength
attributes.description: Measured magnetic field strength at this survey point, expressed in nanoTesla (nT). Used to assess potential magnetic interference that could affect survey accuracy.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this survey record was last modified or updated in the Geovia GEMS system. Used for data lineage and change tracking.

attributes.name: northing_coordinate
attributes.description: Calculated northing (Y) coordinate of this survey point in the mine coordinate system, derived from collar position and survey trajectory. Used for 3D spatial positioning in GIS and block models.

attributes.name: qaqc_status
attributes.description: Current status of quality assurance and quality control validation for this survey record. Indicates whether the data has been reviewed and approved for use in geological modeling.

attributes.name: survey_date
attributes.description: Date on which this downhole survey measurement was captured. Used for temporal tracking and correlation with drilling progress.

attributes.name: survey_instrument
attributes.description: Specific make and model of the survey instrument used to capture this reading (e.g., Reflex EZ-TRAC, Gyrodata MGTS). Important for quality assurance and data validation.

attributes.name: survey_method
attributes.description: Type of survey instrument or technique used to capture this directional measurement. Determines the accuracy and reliability of the survey data.

attributes.name: survey_quality_code
attributes.description: Quality assessment classification for this survey measurement based on instrument performance, environmental conditions, and validation checks. Determines whether the survey data is suitable for resource estimation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Data Quality and Verification

attributes.name: survey_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential order number of this survey measurement within the drillhole. Used to order survey points from collar to end-of-hole.

attributes.name: temperature_celsius
attributes.description: Downhole temperature at this survey point, measured in degrees Celsius. High temperatures can affect instrument accuracy and require correction factors.

products.name: lithology_log
products.description: Downhole lithological logging records capturing rock type, mineralogy, alteration, texture, colour, grain size, and structural observations at depth intervals along each drillhole. Represents the primary geological description of the subsurface and forms the basis for geological unit interpretation and 3D geological modelling. Logged by geologists in the field and entered into Geovia GEMS. Includes QAQC flags and logging geologist identifier.

attributes.name: lithology_log_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the lithological logging record. Primary key for the lithology log entity.

attributes.name: drill_hole_id
attributes.description: Reference to the drill hole in which this lithological observation was recorded. Links this log entry to the parent drill hole entity.

attributes.name: geological_domain_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.geological_domain. Business justification: Lithology log intervals are assigned to geological domains for resource estimation. Currently lithology_log stores domain_code as a STRING; this should be normalized to FK to geological_domain.geologi

attributes.name: geological_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.geological_unit. Business justification: Lithology logs reference standardized geological units from the geological_unit reference catalog. Currently lithology_log stores geological_unit as a STRING; this should be normalized to FK to geolog

attributes.name: logging_geologist_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Geological logging is a regulated activity requiring competent person sign-off for JORC/NI 43-101 compliance. Linking to employee enables competency verification, training currency checks, and audit t

attributes.name: alteration_intensity
attributes.description: Degree or intensity of alteration affecting the rock unit. Ranges from none to pervasive and influences rock competence and processing behavior.

attributes.name: alteration_type
attributes.description: Type of hydrothermal or weathering alteration affecting the rock unit (e.g., sericitic, chloritic, argillic, propylitic). Important for understanding ore genesis and processing characteristics.

attributes.name: colour
attributes.description: Observed colour of the rock unit. Provides visual identification characteristics and may correlate with mineralogy or alteration.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Additional free-text comments or observations recorded by the logging geologist. Captures contextual information that does not fit structured fields.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this lithology log record was first created in the system. Provides audit trail for data governance and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Source system or database from which this lithological log record originated (e.g., Geovia GEMS, field logging tablet). Provides data lineage for integration and reconciliation.

attributes.name: grain_size
attributes.description: Average grain size of the rock matrix, classified according to standard grain size scales. Influences rock strength and processing characteristics.

attributes.name: hardness
attributes.description: Relative hardness of the rock unit assessed by field tests. Provides indication of rock competence and drilling characteristics.

attributes.name: interval_from_depth_m
attributes.description: Starting depth of the logged interval measured in metres from the drill hole collar. Defines the top boundary of the lithological unit being described.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: interval_length_m
attributes.description: Length of the logged interval in metres, calculated as the difference between to_depth and from_depth. Represents the thickness of the lithological unit.

attributes.name: interval_to_depth_m
attributes.description: Ending depth of the logged interval measured in metres from the drill hole collar. Defines the bottom boundary of the lithological unit being described.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: lithology_code
attributes.description: Detailed lithological classification code representing the specific lithological unit or formation. More granular than rock_type_code and aligned with the geological model nomenclature.

attributes.name: lithology_description
attributes.description: Comprehensive free-text description of the lithological characteristics including texture, structure, mineralogy, alteration, weathering, and any other relevant geological observations made by the logging geologist.

attributes.name: logging_date
attributes.description: Date on which the lithological logging was performed. Important for data provenance and temporal tracking of geological interpretation evolution.

attributes.name: logging_method
attributes.description: Method used to perform the lithological logging (e.g., visual inspection, digital logging, photographic logging). Affects data quality and consistency.

attributes.name: mineralisation_type
attributes.description: Style or morphology of mineralisation observed in the interval. Critical for understanding ore body geometry and grade distribution.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this lithology log record was last modified. Tracks data currency and supports change management processes.

attributes.name: oxidation_state
attributes.description: Oxidation state of the rock unit indicating the degree of supergene alteration. Critical for metallurgical processing route selection and resource classification.

attributes.name: primary_mineral
attributes.description: Dominant mineral species observed in the interval. Represents the most abundant mineral constituent of the rock unit.

attributes.name: qaqc_comments
attributes.description: Comments or notes from the quality control review process. Documents any issues, corrections, or validation decisions made during QAQC review.

attributes.name: qaqc_status
attributes.description: Quality control status of the lithological log entry indicating whether it has been validated, requires review, or has been rejected. Critical for data governance and compliance with JORC reporting standards.

attributes.name: recovery_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of core recovered from the drilled interval. High recovery indicates competent rock; low recovery may indicate fractured, weathered, or weak zones. Critical quality control metric.

attributes.name: rock_type_code
attributes.description: Standardized code representing the primary rock type observed in this interval (e.g., GRAN for granite, BAS for basalt, SEDS for sedimentary). Used for geological classification and modeling.

attributes.name: rock_type_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the rock type including lithological characteristics, composition, and geological interpretation. Provides full context beyond the standardized code.

attributes.name: rqd_percent
attributes.description: Rock Quality Designation expressed as percentage of intact core pieces greater than 10cm in length. Standard geotechnical parameter for rock mass quality assessment.

attributes.name: secondary_mineral
attributes.description: Second most abundant mineral species observed in the interval. Provides additional mineralogical context for geological interpretation.

attributes.name: structure
attributes.description: Structural features observed in the interval including bedding, foliation, jointing, veining, or other geological structures. Important for geotechnical and structural geological interpretation.

attributes.name: sulphide_percent
attributes.description: Visual estimate of sulphide mineral content as percentage of the interval. Important for ore grade estimation and metallurgical characterisation.

attributes.name: texture
attributes.description: Textural characteristics of the rock including fabric, grain relationships, and structural features (e.g., porphyritic, aphanitic, foliated, massive).

attributes.name: vein_type
attributes.description: Description of vein characteristics including composition, orientation, and morphology (e.g., quartz vein, calcite vein, tension gash). Relevant for structural and mineralisation interpretation.

attributes.name: veining_percent
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of the interval occupied by veins or veinlets. Important for understanding structural controls on mineralisation and rock mass characteristics.

attributes.name: weathering_degree
attributes.description: Extent of weathering affecting the rock unit, classified according to standard weathering scales. Critical for geotechnical assessment and mine planning.

products.name: structural_measurement
products.description: Records of structural geology measurements captured from drillhole core and surface mapping including orientation data (dip, dip direction, strike), structural feature type (fault, fold, joint, shear zone, vein, foliation), alpha and beta angles, and structural domain assignment. Critical for geomechanical modelling, pit slope design, and understanding structural controls on mineralisation. Sourced from core logging in Geovia GEMS.
products.reference: ISRM Suggested Methods for Rock Characterisation

attributes.name: structural_measurement_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the structural measurement record. Primary key.

attributes.name: drill_hole_id
attributes.description: Reference to the drill hole from which this structural measurement was captured.

attributes.name: geologist_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Structural measurements require geologist accountability for JORC/NI 43-101 compliance and geotechnical data quality audits. Links enable competency verification for structural geology interpretation

attributes.name: alpha_angle
attributes.description: The alpha angle representing the orientation of the structural feature relative to the drill hole axis, used in oriented core analysis.

attributes.name: alteration_type
attributes.description: Type of alteration associated with the structural feature (e.g., silicification, chloritization, sericitization).

attributes.name: beta_angle
attributes.description: The beta angle representing the orientation of the structural feature relative to the drill hole axis, used in oriented core analysis.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Additional comments or notes about the structural measurement, including any anomalies or special observations.

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: The spatial reference system used for the coordinate data (e.g., MGA94 Zone 50, WGS84 UTM Zone 51S).

attributes.name: data_classification
attributes.description: The classification level of this structural measurement data for information security and access control purposes.

attributes.name: dip
attributes.description: The angle of inclination of the structural feature measured downward from the horizontal plane, in degrees (0-90).

attributes.name: dip_direction
attributes.description: The azimuth direction in which the structural feature dips, measured in degrees from north (0-360).

attributes.name: easting
attributes.description: The easting coordinate of the measurement location in the project coordinate system, used for GIS-referenced spatial data.

attributes.name: elevation
attributes.description: The elevation of the measurement location in meters above mean sea level.

attributes.name: feature_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the structural feature including characteristics such as thickness, infill material, surface texture, and any other relevant observations.

attributes.name: feature_thickness
attributes.description: The measured thickness of the structural feature in millimeters (e.g., vein width, fault gouge thickness).

attributes.name: geomechanical_significance
attributes.description: Assessment of the geomechanical significance of the structural feature for pit slope design and ground stability analysis.

attributes.name: infill_material
attributes.description: Description of the material filling the structural feature (e.g., quartz, calcite, clay, gouge).

attributes.name: measurement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the structural measurement was captured in the field or from core logging.

attributes.name: measurement_depth_from
attributes.description: The starting depth in meters down the drill hole where the structural feature was measured. Null for surface measurements.

attributes.name: measurement_depth_to
attributes.description: The ending depth in meters down the drill hole where the structural feature was measured. Null for surface measurements.

attributes.name: measurement_method
attributes.description: The method or instrument used to capture the structural measurement.

attributes.name: measurement_source
attributes.description: The source from which the structural measurement was obtained (drillhole core, surface mapping, underground mapping, outcrop, or trench).

attributes.name: mineralisation_association
attributes.description: Indicates whether the structural feature is associated with mineralisation, critical for understanding structural controls on ore bodies.

attributes.name: northing
attributes.description: The northing coordinate of the measurement location in the project coordinate system, used for GIS-referenced spatial data.

attributes.name: quality_code
attributes.description: Quality assessment of the structural measurement based on exposure quality, measurement accuracy, and confidence.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this structural measurement record was first created in the source system.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this structural measurement record was last updated in the source system.

attributes.name: roughness
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the surface roughness of the structural feature, important for geomechanical modeling.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The system from which this structural measurement record was sourced (e.g., Geovia GEMS, field logging application).

attributes.name: strike
attributes.description: The compass direction of a horizontal line on the plane of the structural feature, measured in degrees from north (0-360).

attributes.name: structural_domain
attributes.description: The structural domain or zone to which this measurement is assigned, representing areas with similar structural characteristics.

attributes.name: structural_feature_type
attributes.description: The type of structural geological feature being measured (fault, fold, joint, shear zone, vein, or foliation).

attributes.name: weathering_state
attributes.description: The degree of weathering observed on the structural feature surface.

products.name: geotechnical_log
products.description: Downhole geotechnical, physical property, and density logging records from diamond drillhole core. Captures rock quality designation (RQD), core recovery, fracture frequency, rock strength (UCS), point load index, rock mass rating (RMR), Q-index, geomechanical domain classification, and all density/specific gravity measurements (water immersion, wax-coated, dry bulk, pycnometer methods) with moisture content at depth intervals. Density records include measurement method, laboratory identifier, geological unit, oxidation state, and QAQC flags. Feeds pit slope stability analysis, underground stope design, ground support specification, and provides density inputs for resource tonnage calculations. Sourced from Geovia GEMS and LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: geotechnical_log_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the geotechnical log record. Primary key for downhole geotechnical and physical property measurements from diamond drillhole core.

attributes.name: drill_hole_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the diamond drillhole from which this geotechnical core sample was extracted. Links to the drill hole master record in the exploration domain.

attributes.name: geological_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.geological_unit. Business justification: Geotechnical logs capture physical properties for specific lithologies. Currently geotechnical_log stores lithology_code as a STRING; this should be normalized to FK to geological_unit.geological_unit

attributes.name: laboratory_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the laboratory facility that performed the geotechnical testing and density measurements. Used for QAQC traceability and inter-laboratory comparison.

attributes.name: logged_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Geotechnical data collection requires competent person accountability for rock mechanics studies, slope stability analysis, and mine design. Links enable competency verification and audit trails for s

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for geotechnical observations, notes on core condition, structural features, alteration, or any other relevant geomechanical information not captured in structured fields.

attributes.name: core_recovery_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of core recovered from the drilled interval, calculated as (recovered core length / drilled interval length) × 100. Critical indicator of rock quality and drilling conditions.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Source system from which this geotechnical log record was extracted. Typically Geovia GEMS for geological logging or LabWare LIMS for laboratory density and strength testing results.

attributes.name: density_measurement_method
attributes.description: Laboratory method used to determine density and specific gravity. Water immersion is standard for competent core; wax-coated method used for porous or friable samples; pycnometer for fine material.

attributes.name: depth_from
attributes.description: Starting depth in meters downhole from collar for this geotechnical measurement interval. Defines the top of the logged interval.

attributes.name: depth_to
attributes.description: Ending depth in meters downhole from collar for this geotechnical measurement interval. Defines the bottom of the logged interval.

attributes.name: dry_bulk_density
attributes.description: Dry bulk density of the core sample in tonnes per cubic meter, measured after oven-drying to constant mass. Primary density value for resource tonnage calculations.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 3 Estimation and Reporting

attributes.name: fracture_frequency
attributes.description: Number of natural fractures, joints, or discontinuities per meter of core. Key parameter for rock mass characterization and ground support design.

attributes.name: geomechanical_domain
attributes.description: Geomechanical domain classification code representing zones of similar rock mass behavior. Used to group rock masses with consistent geotechnical properties for slope stability and stope design modeling.

attributes.name: interval_length
attributes.description: Length of the geotechnical logging interval in meters, calculated as depth_to minus depth_from. Represents the core run length for this measurement.

attributes.name: logging_date
attributes.description: Date when the geotechnical core logging was performed in the field or core shed. Distinct from laboratory test date.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling and Sub-sampling

attributes.name: moisture_content_percent
attributes.description: Moisture content of the sample at time of measurement, calculated as ((wet mass - dry mass) / dry mass) × 100. Used to convert between wet and dry density values.
attributes.references: ASTM D2216 - Laboratory Determination of Water Content

attributes.name: oxidation_state
attributes.description: Degree of oxidation and weathering of the rock mass per ISRM weathering classification. Critical for density correction and geotechnical property correlation.

attributes.name: point_load_index_mpa
attributes.description: Point Load Strength Index corrected to 50mm diameter equivalent (Is50) in megapascals. Field-based rock strength indicator used to estimate UCS when core testing is not available.
attributes.references: ISRM Suggested Methods - Point Load Test

attributes.name: porosity_percent
attributes.description: Porosity of the rock sample expressed as percentage of void space to total volume. Influences density, strength, and fluid flow characteristics.

attributes.name: q_index
attributes.description: Tunneling Quality Index (Q-system) per Barton et al. (1974). Logarithmic rock mass classification calculated from RQD, joint set number, joint roughness, joint alteration, water reduction factor, and stress reduction factor. Used for underground excavation support design.

attributes.name: qaqc_flag
attributes.description: Free-text quality control flag or comment describing any data quality issues, anomalies, or validation failures identified during QAQC review. Empty if no issues detected.

attributes.name: qaqc_status
attributes.description: Quality assurance and quality control validation status for this geotechnical record. Indicates whether the data has passed internal validation checks for completeness, consistency, and accuracy.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this geotechnical log record was first created in the source system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this geotechnical log record was last modified in the source system. Used for change tracking and incremental data loading.

attributes.name: rmr_rating
attributes.description: Rock Mass Rating classification value (0-100 scale) per Bieniawski (1989). Composite geomechanical classification integrating rock strength, RQD, discontinuity spacing, condition, groundwater, and orientation. Used for ground support design.

attributes.name: rqd_percent
attributes.description: Rock Quality Designation percentage, calculated as the sum of intact core pieces greater than 100mm divided by total interval length × 100. Standard geotechnical index for rock mass quality per Deere (1964).

attributes.name: sample_number
attributes.description: Unique laboratory sample number assigned to the core interval for geotechnical testing. Links to sample chain-of-custody and laboratory information management system.

attributes.name: specific_gravity
attributes.description: Specific gravity of the rock sample, representing the ratio of sample density to water density. Measured using water immersion, wax-coated, or pycnometer methods.
attributes.references: ASTM D854 - Specific Gravity of Soil Solids

attributes.name: test_date
attributes.description: Date when the geotechnical laboratory testing was performed. Critical for temporal QAQC analysis and data vintage tracking.

attributes.name: ucs_mpa
attributes.description: Unconfined Compressive Strength of intact rock measured in megapascals (MPa). Laboratory-determined strength of rock under uniaxial compression, critical for pit slope and stope design.
attributes.references: ISRM Suggested Methods - Uniaxial Compressive Strength

attributes.name: wet_bulk_density
attributes.description: Wet bulk density of the core sample in tonnes per cubic meter, measured at natural moisture content. Used for in-situ tonnage estimation and comparison with dry density.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 3 Estimation and Reporting

products.name: block_model
products.description: Master register of 3D block model instances representing the geological and grade model of each orebody, with full version control. Captures model name, version identifier, block dimensions (X, Y, Z rotation), parent block size, sub-blocking configuration, coordinate system, datum, creation date, estimation method, model status (active, superseded, archived), version date, reason for update (new drilling, reinterpretation, methodology change), key changes summary, competent person sign-off, approval status, and superseded version reference. Each block model instance is the container for all block-level attribute data used in resource estimation and mine planning. Version history ensures full audit trail for JORC-compliant resource reporting and regulatory disclosure. Sourced from Geovia GEMS.
products.reference: Geovia GEMS Block Model Standard; JORC Geological Modelling

attributes.name: block_model_id
attributes.description: Primary key for block_model

attributes.name: capital_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to project.capital_project. Business justification: Block models are created to support specific capital projects for pit optimization, plant sizing, and mine planning. Feasibility studies and stage gate reviews reference block models for tonnage/grade

attributes.name: competent_person_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the competent person who signed off on this block model version. Links to the competent person register.

attributes.name: orebody_id
attributes.description: FK to geology.orebody

attributes.name: primary_superseded_by_model_block_model_id
attributes.description: Reference to the block model version that superseded this version. Null for active models. Enables version chain navigation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Governance and Internal Controls

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Block model creation is a capital project deliverable with significant costs (drilling campaigns, geological consulting, software). Mining companies track geological modeling costs through WBS for cap

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when this block model version was formally approved by the competent person and management.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Governance and Internal Controls

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Approval status of this block model version. Indicates whether the model has been formally approved by the competent person and management for use in resource reporting and mine planning.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Governance and Internal Controls

attributes.name: commodity_type
attributes.description: Primary commodity or mineral type modeled in this block model (e.g., iron ore, copper, coal, lithium, nickel). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: iron_ore|copper|coal|lithium|nickel|gold|silver|zinc|lead|bauxite|other — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: Coordinate reference system used for the block model (e.g., 'MGA Zone 50', 'WGS84 UTM Zone 33S', 'NAD83 State Plane'). Defines the spatial reference framework.

attributes.name: data_cutoff_date
attributes.description: Date up to which drilling and sampling data were included in this block model. Defines the temporal scope of input data.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: datum
attributes.description: Geodetic datum used for the block model (e.g., 'GDA94', 'WGS84', 'NAD83'). Defines the reference ellipsoid and origin for coordinate measurements.

attributes.name: drill_hole_count
attributes.description: Number of drill holes used as input data for this block model version. Indicates the density of sampling data.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Statistical method used for grade estimation in this block model (e.g., ordinary kriging, inverse distance weighting, nearest neighbor, indicator kriging). Critical for JORC compliance and resource classification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ordinary_kriging|inverse_distance|nearest_neighbor|indicator_kriging|multiple_indicator_kriging|uniform_conditioning|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 3 Estimation and Reporting of Mineral Resources

attributes.name: estimation_software
attributes.description: Software package used to create and populate the block model (e.g., 'Geovia GEMS 6.8', 'Datamine Studio RM 1.8', 'Leapfrog Geo 2023.1').
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 3 Estimation and Reporting of Mineral Resources

attributes.name: extent_x
attributes.description: Total extent of the block model in the X direction (easting) in meters. Defines the overall model width.

attributes.name: extent_y
attributes.description: Total extent of the block model in the Y direction (northing) in meters. Defines the overall model length.

attributes.name: extent_z
attributes.description: Total extent of the block model in the Z direction (elevation) in meters. Defines the overall model height.

attributes.name: key_changes_summary
attributes.description: Summary of key changes made in this version compared to the previous version. Provides context for version history and audit trail.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Governance and Internal Controls

attributes.name: model_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier or code for the block model, used for external reference and reporting (e.g., 'NPT_IO_2024_V3', 'SCD_CU_2023_V1').

attributes.name: model_name
attributes.description: Business name of the block model instance, typically referencing the orebody or deposit name (e.g., 'North Pit Iron Ore Model', 'South Copper Deposit Model').

attributes.name: model_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the block model instance. Active models are used for current planning and resource estimation; superseded models have been replaced by newer versions; archived models are retained for historical reference; draft models are under development; under_review models are pending validation; approved models have passed competent person sign-off.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Governance and Internal Controls

attributes.name: origin_x
attributes.description: X-coordinate (easting) of the block model origin point in the specified coordinate system. Defines the southwest corner of the model grid.

attributes.name: origin_y
attributes.description: Y-coordinate (northing) of the block model origin point in the specified coordinate system. Defines the southwest corner of the model grid.

attributes.name: origin_z
attributes.description: Z-coordinate (elevation) of the block model origin point in meters above the datum. Defines the base elevation of the model grid.

attributes.name: parent_block_size_x
attributes.description: X-axis dimension (easting) of the parent block in meters. Defines the fundamental block size in the east-west direction.

attributes.name: parent_block_size_y
attributes.description: Y-axis dimension (northing) of the parent block in meters. Defines the fundamental block size in the north-south direction.

attributes.name: parent_block_size_z
attributes.description: Z-axis dimension (elevation) of the parent block in meters. Defines the fundamental block size in the vertical direction.

attributes.name: rotation_angle
attributes.description: Rotation angle of the block model grid in degrees, measured clockwise from north. Used to align the model with the orebody strike direction.

attributes.name: sample_count
attributes.description: Total number of assay samples used as input data for this block model version. Indicates the volume of analytical data.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: sub_block_configuration
attributes.description: Description of the sub-blocking configuration if enabled (e.g., '2x2x2', '4x4x4', 'adaptive'). Specifies how parent blocks are subdivided.

attributes.name: sub_blocking_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether sub-blocking (subdivision of parent blocks into smaller blocks) is enabled in this model to improve resolution at orebody boundaries and geological contacts.

attributes.name: superseded_date
attributes.description: Date when this block model version was superseded by a newer version. Null for active models.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Governance and Internal Controls

attributes.name: total_block_count
attributes.description: Total number of blocks (parent and sub-blocks) in the block model. Used for model size assessment and computational planning.

attributes.name: update_reason
attributes.description: Primary reason for creating this new version of the block model (e.g., new drilling data, geological reinterpretation, methodology change, data correction, resource update, mine depletion). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new_drilling|geological_reinterpretation|methodology_change|data_correction|resource_update|mine_depletion|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 3 Estimation and Reporting of Mineral Resources

attributes.name: version_date
attributes.description: Effective date of this block model version. Represents the date from which this version is considered current for resource reporting and mine planning.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Governance and Internal Controls

attributes.name: version_identifier
attributes.description: Version number or identifier for this block model instance (e.g., 'V1', 'V2.1', '2024.03'). Used to track model evolution and updates.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Governance and Internal Controls

attributes.name: creation_date
attributes.description: Date when this block model version was created. Used for version control and audit trail.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Governance and Internal Controls

products.name: block_model_cell
products.description: Individual block (cell) records within a 3D block model, each representing a discrete volumetric unit of the orebody model. Captures block centroid coordinates (X, Y, Z), block dimensions, geological domain code, lithological unit, estimated grade by commodity (Fe%, Cu ppm, Au g/t, etc.), density, rock type, oxidation state, ore/waste classification, and modifying factor flags. The fundamental unit of resource estimation and mine planning optimisation. Sourced from Geovia GEMS block model exports.
products.reference: Geovia GEMS Block Model Cell Attributes

attributes.name: block_model_cell_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the block model cell. Primary key for the block model cell entity.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, CIM Definition Standards

attributes.name: block_model_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent block model to which this cell belongs. Links to the specific geological model version and configuration.

attributes.name: geological_domain_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.geological_domain. Business justification: Block model cells are classified into geological domains for resource estimation. The cell currently stores geological_domain_code as a STRING; this should be normalized to a FK to geological_domain.g

attributes.name: geological_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.geological_unit. Business justification: block_model_cell currently has lithology_code and rock_type as STRING attributes. These are denormalized references to the geological_unit reference catalog. Adding geological_unit_id FK normalizes th

attributes.name: pit_design_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the optimized pit shell that contains this block. Used for open pit mine planning and scheduling. Links to pit optimization scenarios.

attributes.name: saleable_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.saleable_product. Business justification: Block model cells classified as ore are assigned to specific saleable products based on grade and quality specifications. Critical for mine-to-mill optimization, production scheduling, product forecas

attributes.name: block_dimension_x
attributes.description: Width of the block in the X direction (easting) measured in meters. Defines the block size in the east-west dimension.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Geovia GEMS Block Model Standards

attributes.name: block_dimension_y
attributes.description: Length of the block in the Y direction (northing) measured in meters. Defines the block size in the north-south dimension.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Geovia GEMS Block Model Standards

attributes.name: block_dimension_z
attributes.description: Height of the block in the Z direction (elevation) measured in meters. Defines the vertical block size.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Geovia GEMS Block Model Standards

attributes.name: block_volume_m3
attributes.description: Volume of the block in cubic meters. Calculated as the product of block dimensions (X * Y * Z) and used for tonnage calculations.

attributes.name: centroid_x
attributes.description: X coordinate of the block centroid in the mine coordinate system (easting). Represents the center point of the block in the east-west direction.
attributes.references: GIS (Geographic Information System) Standards, JORC Code

attributes.name: centroid_y
attributes.description: Y coordinate of the block centroid in the mine coordinate system (northing). Represents the center point of the block in the north-south direction.
attributes.references: GIS (Geographic Information System) Standards, JORC Code

attributes.name: centroid_z
attributes.description: Z coordinate of the block centroid representing elevation or depth below surface. Vertical position of the block center in the mine coordinate system.
attributes.references: GIS (Geographic Information System) Standards, JORC Code

attributes.name: cut_off_grade_applied
attributes.description: The minimum economic grade threshold applied to classify this block as ore or waste. Critical parameter for resource-to-reserve conversion and mine planning optimization.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Mine Planning Standards

attributes.name: density_t_per_m3
attributes.description: Bulk density of the block material measured in tonnes per cubic meter. Used to convert block volume to tonnage for resource estimation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, CIM Definition Standards

attributes.name: dilution_factor
attributes.description: Expected dilution factor representing the proportion of waste material mixed with ore during mining. Modifying factor applied during reserve conversion.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Mine Planning Standards

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Geostatistical method used to estimate grades for this block. Documents the interpolation technique applied during resource modeling.

attributes.name: estimation_pass
attributes.description: The estimation pass number during which this block was populated. Multi-pass estimation uses progressively relaxed search parameters to fill all blocks.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Geovia GEMS Standards

attributes.name: grade_au_g_per_t
attributes.description: Estimated gold (Au) grade within the block expressed in grams per tonne. Critical for precious metal deposits and by-product recovery.

attributes.name: grade_coal_ash_pct
attributes.description: Estimated ash content percentage for coal blocks. Key quality parameter for coal deposits affecting market value and processing requirements.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Coal Quality Standards

attributes.name: grade_coal_sulfur_pct
attributes.description: Estimated sulfur content percentage for coal blocks. Environmental and quality parameter affecting coal marketability and emissions.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Coal Quality Standards

attributes.name: grade_cu_ppm
attributes.description: Estimated copper (Cu) grade within the block expressed in parts per million (ppm). Used for copper and polymetallic deposits.

attributes.name: grade_fe_pct
attributes.description: Estimated iron (Fe) grade within the block expressed as a percentage. Primary commodity grade for iron ore deposits.

attributes.name: grade_li_ppm
attributes.description: Estimated lithium (Li) grade within the block expressed in parts per million (ppm). Used for lithium brine and hard rock deposits.

attributes.name: grade_ni_pct
attributes.description: Estimated nickel (Ni) grade within the block expressed as a percentage. Primary commodity grade for nickel deposits.

attributes.name: kriging_variance
attributes.description: Statistical variance from kriging estimation for this block. Measure of estimation uncertainty and confidence in the grade estimate.

attributes.name: mining_method_flag
attributes.description: Planned or applicable mining method for extracting this block. Values include open_pit, underground, SLC (Sub-Level Caving), block_cave, longwall (coal), room_pillar, not_applicable. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: open_pit|underground|slc|block_cave|longwall|room_pillar|not_applicable — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Mine Planning Standards

attributes.name: mining_phase
attributes.description: Planned mining phase or stage in which this block is scheduled for extraction. Used for Life of Mine (LOM) planning and sequencing.

attributes.name: mining_recovery_factor
attributes.description: Expected mining recovery factor representing the proportion of in-situ ore that can be extracted. Modifying factor applied during reserve conversion.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Mine Planning Standards

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the block model. Tracks model updates and revisions over time as new geological data becomes available.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: number_of_samples
attributes.description: Count of drill hole samples used to estimate grades for this block. Indicator of estimation confidence and data density.

attributes.name: ore_waste_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the block as ore, waste, or intermediate material based on cut-off grade criteria. Drives mine planning and scheduling decisions.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Mine Planning Standards

attributes.name: oxidation_state
attributes.description: Oxidation state of the ore within the block. Critical for determining processing method and recovery rates. Values: oxide (weathered), transitional (mixed), fresh (unweathered), supergene (secondary enrichment), hypogene (primary).
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Mineral Processing Standards

attributes.name: processing_recovery_factor
attributes.description: Expected metallurgical recovery factor representing the proportion of valuable mineral that can be recovered during processing. Modifying factor applied during reserve conversion.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, Mineral Processing Standards

attributes.name: reserve_category
attributes.description: JORC/NI 43-101 ore reserve classification category for this block after applying modifying factors. Proved (highest confidence), probable (moderate confidence), not_reserve (does not meet economic criteria), unclassified.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, NI 43-101, SEC S-K 1300

attributes.name: resource_category
attributes.description: JORC/NI 43-101 resource classification category for this block. Reflects confidence level in the geological and grade continuity: measured (highest confidence), indicated (moderate confidence), inferred (lowest confidence), unclassified (insufficient data).
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, NI 43-101, SEC S-K 1300

attributes.name: tonnage
attributes.description: Total tonnage of material within the block, calculated as volume multiplied by density. Fundamental metric for resource and reserve reporting.

products.name: grade_control_sample
products.description: Grade control sampling records from blast holes, channel samples, trench samples, and face samples taken during active mining operations to define ore/waste boundaries for short-term mine planning and dig-line delineation. Captures sample identifier, spatial location (easting, northing, RL, bench, pit, mining block), sample type, interval length, assay results by commodity (Fe%, Cu ppm, Au g/t), ore type classification, material destination (crusher, ROM pad, stockpile, waste dump), reconciliation flag against the block model prediction, and grade control geologist sign-off. The operational bridge between the long-term geological model and daily mining execution — enables model-vs-actual reconciliation. Sourced from LabWare LIMS and Geovia GEMS grade control modules.

attributes.name: grade_control_sample_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the grade control sample record. Primary key for the grade control sample entity.

attributes.name: blast_pattern_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the blast pattern from which the sample was collected. Links grade control samples to specific drilling and blasting operations for reconciliation.

attributes.name: block_model_cell_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.block_model_cell. Business justification: Grade control samples validate specific block model cell predictions. Required for ore/waste classification decisions, model confidence assessment, and identifying areas requiring infill sampling.

attributes.name: block_model_id

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Grade control sampling is an operational cost (drilling, assaying, geological labor) allocated to cost centres for ore control activities. Essential for mining opex tracking, AISC calculation, and uni

attributes.name: drill_rig_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to equipment.asset. Business justification: Grade control sampling operations must track which drill rig collected each sample for sample integrity verification, QAQC traceability, and correlation of sample quality with equipment performance. C

attributes.name: geologist_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Grade control decisions (ore/waste classification) require geologist sign-off for production accountability and reconciliation. Links enable competency verification, production variance analysis, and

attributes.name: laboratory_sample_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.laboratory_sample. Business justification: Grade control samples are collected from production drilling/blasting and sent to laboratory for assay. Links mining execution to laboratory analysis for ore/waste classification and production reconc

attributes.name: orebody_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.orebody. Business justification: Grade control samples are collected from specific orebodies during production. Currently grade_control_sample has pit_name and mining_block but no direct orebody link. Adding orebody_id FK enables dir

attributes.name: production_drillhole_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific blast hole or drill hole from which the sample was collected. Used for blast hole samples to link back to drilling operations.

attributes.name: saleable_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.saleable_product. Business justification: Grade control samples determine real-time material destination to specific saleable products based on assay results meeting product specifications. Essential for ore routing decisions, stockpile alloc

attributes.name: al2o3_percent
attributes.description: Assayed alumina content of the sample expressed as a percentage. Key deleterious element for iron ore quality and processing.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Assay Standard - Deleterious Elements

attributes.name: assay_completion_date
attributes.description: Date when the laboratory completed the assay analysis and reported results. Used to track turnaround time and operational delays.

attributes.name: assay_method
attributes.description: Analytical method used for sample assay. Examples include XRF (X-Ray Fluorescence), fire assay, ICP-MS (Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry), AAS (Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy). Critical for quality control and data validation.

attributes.name: au_g_per_t
attributes.description: Assayed gold content of the sample expressed in grams per tonne. Critical commodity grade for gold operations and by-product recovery.

attributes.name: bench
attributes.description: Identifier of the mining bench or level where the sample was collected. Benches are horizontal working surfaces in open pit mines, typically designated by elevation (e.g., 450RL, 440RL).

attributes.name: block_model_grade
attributes.description: Predicted grade from the long-term geological block model for the spatial location of this sample. Used for model-versus-actual reconciliation to assess geological model accuracy.

attributes.name: collection_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the grade control sample was physically collected in the field during mining operations. Critical for temporal reconciliation and operational sequencing.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for geologist observations, sample collection notes, geological features, contamination issues, or any other relevant contextual information about the sample.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this grade control sample record was first created in the database. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: cu_ppm
attributes.description: Assayed copper content of the sample expressed in parts per million. Key commodity grade for copper operations.

attributes.name: easting
attributes.description: East-west spatial coordinate of the sample location in the mine grid coordinate system, typically in meters. Used for GIS mapping and spatial reconciliation against the geological block model.

attributes.name: elevation_rl
attributes.description: Vertical elevation of the sample location relative to a defined datum, typically in meters above sea level. RL (Reduced Level) is the mining industry standard term for elevation.

attributes.name: fe_percent
attributes.description: Assayed iron content of the sample expressed as a percentage of total mass. Primary commodity grade for iron ore operations.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Assay Standard - Iron Ore

attributes.name: geologist_sign_off_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the grade control geologist formally validated and signed off on the sample data and classification. Critical for operational approval workflow.

attributes.name: grade_variance
attributes.description: Calculated difference between the assayed grade and the block model predicted grade. Positive values indicate actual grade exceeded prediction, negative values indicate under-prediction. Key metric for geological model reconciliation.

attributes.name: interval_length
attributes.description: Length of the sample interval in meters, calculated as the difference between interval_to and interval_from. Represents the vertical or horizontal extent of material represented by the sample.

attributes.name: laboratory_name
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the laboratory that performed the assay analysis. May be on-site laboratory or external commercial laboratory.

attributes.name: material_destination
attributes.description: Designated destination for the material represented by this sample based on grade control classification. Crusher for direct processing, ROM (Run of Mine) pad for temporary storage before processing, stockpile for longer-term ore storage, waste dump for sub-economic material.

attributes.name: mining_block
attributes.description: Short-term mining block identifier representing the operational dig unit. Mining blocks are subdivisions of the pit used for daily to weekly mine planning and grade control.

attributes.name: northing
attributes.description: North-south spatial coordinate of the sample location in the mine grid coordinate system, typically in meters. Used for GIS mapping and spatial reconciliation against the geological block model.

attributes.name: ore_type
attributes.description: Geological classification of the ore type based on mineralogy, lithology, and processing characteristics. Examples include hematite, magnetite, banded iron formation, oxide copper, sulfide copper, free-milling gold. Used for material routing and processing decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: hematite|magnetite|goethite|bif|oxide_cu|sulfide_cu|transitional_cu|free_milling_au|refractory_au — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS Ore Type Classification Standard

attributes.name: p_percent
attributes.description: Assayed phosphorus content of the sample expressed as a percentage. Critical deleterious element for steel-making iron ore quality.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Assay Standard - Deleterious Elements

attributes.name: pit_name
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the open pit mine where the sample was collected. Used to segment grade control data by mining area.

attributes.name: qaqc_status

attributes.name: reconciliation_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this sample has been included in formal mine-to-model reconciliation reporting. True indicates the sample has been reconciled, false indicates pending reconciliation.

attributes.name: s_percent
attributes.description: Assayed sulfur content of the sample expressed as a percentage. Key deleterious element for iron ore and copper concentrate quality.

attributes.name: sample_interval_from
attributes.description: Starting depth of the sample interval in meters, measured from the collar of the hole. Used for blast hole and channel samples to define the vertical extent of the sample.

attributes.name: sample_interval_to
attributes.description: Ending depth of the sample interval in meters, measured from the collar of the hole. Used for blast hole and channel samples to define the vertical extent of the sample.

attributes.name: sample_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique sample identifier assigned by the laboratory or field geologist. Used for tracking and reconciliation across systems.

attributes.name: sample_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the grade control sample. Tracks progression from field collection through laboratory assay to final validation and reconciliation against block model predictions.

attributes.name: sample_type
attributes.description: Classification of the grade control sample collection method. attributes.name: sample_weight_kg
attributes.description: Weight of the collected sample in kilograms. Used for quality control and to ensure representative sample mass for laboratory analysis.

attributes.name: sio2_percent

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

Captures domain name, parent orebody, bounding wireframe reference, commodity, estimation constraint type (hard or soft boundary), variogram model parameters, and domain status. attributes.name: competent_person_id

attributes.name: orebody_id

attributes.name: average_grade
attributes.description: Mean grade of the primary commodity across all samples within this geological domain. Used for domain validation and resource reporting.

attributes.name: bulk_density
attributes.description: Average bulk density of the rock within this domain in tonnes per cubic meter. Used to convert volume to tonnage for resource estimation.

attributes.name: domain_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code used to identify the domain in geological models and block models. Typically used in Geovia GEMS domain coding workflows.

attributes.name: domain_name

attributes.name: domain_type

attributes.name: domain_volume_m3

attributes.name: effective_date

attributes.name: geological_confidence

attributes.name: geological_domain_status

attributes.name: grade_variance

attributes.name: maximum_sample_count
attributes.description: Maximum number of assay samples used in a single block grade estimation. Prevents over-smoothing and maintains local variability.

attributes.name: minimum_sample_count
attributes.description: Minimum number of assay samples required within the search ellipsoid to estimate a block grade. Ensures statistical reliability of estimates.

attributes.name: model_version

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: resource_category

attributes.name: sample_count
attributes.description: Total number of assay samples (drill hole intercepts, channel samples, etc.) used to define and characterize this geological domain.

attributes.name: search_ellipsoid_azimuth_deg
attributes.description: Azimuth angle in degrees (0-360) defining the orientation of the major axis of the search ellipsoid used in kriging. Typically aligned with geological strike.

attributes.name: search_ellipsoid_dip_deg
attributes.description: Dip angle in degrees (-90 to +90) defining the plunge of the major axis of the search ellipsoid. Typically aligned with orebody dip.

attributes.name: search_ellipsoid_plunge_deg
attributes.description: Plunge angle in degrees (0-360) defining the rotation of the search ellipsoid around the major axis. Used for complex 3D orientations.
attributes.references: CIM Estimation of Mineral Resources and Mineral Reserves Best Practice Guidelines

attributes.name: superseded_date
attributes.description: Date on which this domain definition was superseded by a newer interpretation. Null for active domains. Supports audit trail of geological model evolution.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this geological domain record was last modified. Supports change tracking and data lineage.

attributes.name: variogram_model_type

attributes.name: variogram_nugget_effect

attributes.name: variogram_range_major_m

attributes.name: variogram_range_minor_m

attributes.name: variogram_range_semi_major_m
attributes.description: Range of spatial continuity in the semi-major axis direction (typically across strike or intermediate dimension) in meters.

attributes.name: variogram_sill

attributes.name: centroid_northing

products.name: geostatistical_run
products.description: Records of individual geostatistical estimation runs capturing the full estimation methodology, variogram model, and resource classification output for a specific geological domain and commodity within a block model. Includes compositing parameters (method, length, support correction), variogram model definition (type — spherical/exponential/Gaussian, nugget, sill, range for major/semi-major/minor axes, rotation angles, fitting method), search ellipse configuration, minimum and maximum samples, kriging neighbourhood, estimation method (ordinary kriging, simple kriging, inverse distance, conditional simulation), run date, operator, software version, and validation statistics (slope of regression, kriging efficiency, conditional bias, swath plots). Also captures the resulting resource classification assignment per block (JORC category, classification method, criteria thresholds such as kriging variance, search volume, data spacing, effective date). Provides complete audit trail for resource estimation reproducibility and JORC competent person sign-off. This is the SSOT for all geostatistical parameterisation and classification outputs. Sourced from Geovia GEMS.
