attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: Survey measurements of mined volumes must be attributed to tenements for production reconciliation, royalty calculations, and regulatory reporting. Essential for quarterly production returns and reser

attributes.name: waste_dump_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.waste_dump. Business justification: Surveys measure waste dump volumes. N:1 relationship (many surveys of one dump over time). No bidirectional conflict. Valid operational link.

attributes.name: wireframe_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.wireframe. Business justification: Survey measurements validate as-built geometry against design wireframes. Required for reconciliation, identifying deviations from design, and updating wireframes based on actual mining progress.

attributes.name: accuracy_class
attributes.description: Classification of the positional accuracy standard achieved by the survey method. Survey-grade (±0.05m) is required for production reconciliation; engineering-grade (±0.1–0.5m) for planning; reconnaissance for preliminary assessments.
attributes.references: ISO 19157 — Data Quality; Hexagon MinePlan — Accuracy Standards

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the survey measurement record was formally approved by the authorised mine surveyor. Required for regulatory compliance and production reporting sign-off.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA — Approval Workflow; MSHA — Survey Certification

attributes.name: bulk_density
attributes.description: Bulk density factor in tonnes per cubic metre (t/m³) applied to convert surveyed volume to estimated tonnes. Value may vary by material type (ore, waste, ROM, concentrate) and moisture content.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 — Bulk Density; Geovia GEMS — Density Model

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: The geodetic coordinate reference system (CRS) used for the survey, expressed as an EPSG code or named datum (e.g., GDA2020 / MGA Zone 54, WGS84 UTM). Ensures spatial data interoperability with GIS and Hexagon MinePlan.
attributes.references: ISO 19111 — Spatial Referencing by Coordinates; GIS

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this survey measurement record was first created in the system, including timezone offset. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: ISO 8601 — Date and Time; IFRS 6 — Exploration for and Evaluation of Mineral Resources

attributes.name: design_volume_m3
attributes.description: The planned or design volume in cubic metres (m³) for the surveyed feature as per the mine design model in Hexagon MinePlan or Deswik. Used to calculate variance to design for production scheduling compliance.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Mine Design; Deswik — Schedule Design

attributes.name: dtm_file_ref
attributes.description: File path or object storage URI referencing the Digital Terrain Model (DTM) or Digital Surface Model (DSM) derived from the survey, used as the basis for volume calculations in Hexagon MinePlan.

attributes.name: elevation_max_m
attributes.description: Maximum elevation in metres above Reduced Level (mRL) datum recorded within the survey extent. Used for crest height validation, dump height compliance, and TSF (Tailings Storage Facility) freeboard monitoring.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Elevation Model; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

attributes.name: elevation_min_m
attributes.description: Minimum elevation in metres above Reduced Level (mRL) datum recorded within the survey extent. Used for bench floor validation, geotechnical monitoring, and pit design compliance.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Elevation Model; Geovia GEMS

attributes.name: geotechnical_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this survey measurement was triggered or flagged for geotechnical monitoring purposes (e.g., slope stability monitoring, TSF embankment deformation, underground convergence). When true, the record is shared with the geotechnical team for risk assessment.
attributes.references: IsoMetrix — HSE Risk Assessment; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety

attributes.name: horizontal_accuracy_m
attributes.description: Estimated horizontal positional accuracy of the survey in metres (m), representing the root mean square error (RMSE) of check point comparisons. Governs fitness-for-purpose for production reconciliation and geotechnical monitoring.

attributes.name: material_type
attributes.description: Classification of the primary material type present in the surveyed feature. Distinguishes ore, waste rock, ROM (Run of Mine) material, overburden, tailings, or concentrate stockpiles for production accounting and reconciliation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 — Material Classification; Hexagon MinePlan

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for the surveyor to record observations, anomalies, data quality caveats, or contextual information about the survey event (e.g., partial coverage due to access restrictions, equipment issues, or safety exclusion zones).
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Survey Notes; ISO 19157 Data Quality

attributes.name: point_cloud_file_ref
attributes.description: File path or object storage URI referencing the raw point cloud dataset (LAS/LAZ format) or photogrammetric model generated by the survey. Enables traceability back to source survey data in the data lake.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Survey Data Management; ISO 19157 Data Quality

attributes.name: production_period
attributes.description: The production reporting period (e.g., 2024-Q3, 2024-W42) to which this survey measurement is attributed for production reconciliation and LOM (Life of Mine) schedule tracking.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO — Production Period; Hexagon MinePlan — Schedule Period

attributes.name: strip_ratio
attributes.description: The ratio of waste/overburden volume to ore volume derived from the survey measurement for the period, expressed as bcm waste per tonne of ore. A key open-cut mining efficiency metric used in LOM planning and OPEX (Operating Expenditure) tracking.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 — Strip Ratio; Hexagon MinePlan — Mine Planning

attributes.name: survey_area_m2
attributes.description: Total horizontal surface area in square metres (m²) covered by the survey extent polygon. Used to assess survey coverage completeness and calculate average depth or height of material.

attributes.name: survey_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the physical survey was conducted in the field. This is the principal real-world event date used for production reconciliation and scheduling alignment.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Survey Date; JORC Code 2012

attributes.name: survey_method
attributes.description: The geospatial data capture technique used to conduct the survey. Common methods include drone photogrammetry, LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging), total station, GPS RTK (Real-Time Kinematic), mobile mapping system (MMS), and terrestrial laser scanning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: drone_photogrammetry|lidar|total_station|gps_rtk|mms|laser_scan|handheld_gps|aerial_photogrammetry — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Survey Method; ISO 19115 Geographic Information Metadata

attributes.name: survey_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to the survey event, used for cross-referencing with Hexagon MinePlan survey records, field reports, and production reconciliation documents.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Survey Reference; JORC Code 2012 Table 1

attributes.name: survey_status
attributes.description: Current workflow lifecycle status of the survey measurement record, from initial field capture through review and approval to archival.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Survey Workflow; ISO 19157 Data Quality

attributes.name: survey_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time at which the survey capture commenced, including timezone offset. Used for SCADA integration and time-series alignment with OSIsoft PI System historian data.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System — Event Timestamp; Hexagon MinePlan

attributes.name: survey_type
attributes.description: Classification of the survey target area or structure being measured. Covers open-cut pit floors, waste dumps, ROM (Run of Mine) stockpiles, underground workings, Tailings Storage Facilities (TSF), and haul roads. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pit_floor|dump|stockpile|underground|tsf|haul_road|portal|decline|berm — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Survey Type; JORC Code 2012

attributes.name: surveyed_tonnes
attributes.description: Estimated mass in dry metric tonnes (dmt) of material represented by the surveyed volume, derived by applying the appropriate bulk density factor. Used for production reconciliation against FMS (Fleet Management System) truck counts.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Tonnage Calculation; JORC Code 2012 Bulk Density

attributes.name: surveyed_volume_m3
attributes.description: Total volumetric measurement of the surveyed feature (pit void, stockpile, dump, or underground void) in cubic metres (m³), as calculated from the survey point cloud or digital terrain model (DTM) in Hexagon MinePlan.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Volume Calculation; JORC Code 2012

attributes.name: tonnes_change
attributes.description: Net change in estimated dry metric tonnes between the current and previous survey for the same location. Used as the primary production reconciliation metric against FMS-reported movement tonnes.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Tonnage Reconciliation; Caterpillar MineStar FMS

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this survey measurement record was last modified, including timezone offset. Used for change tracking, incremental data pipeline processing, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 8601 — Date and Time; IFRS 6 — Exploration for and Evaluation of Mineral Resources

attributes.name: variance_to_design_m3
attributes.description: Difference in cubic metres (m³) between the surveyed volume and the design volume (surveyed minus design). Negative values indicate under-excavation; positive values indicate over-excavation or excess material. Critical for LOM (Life of Mine) plan compliance.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Design Variance; Deswik — Schedule Compliance

attributes.name: variance_to_design_pct
attributes.description: Percentage variance between the surveyed volume and the design volume, expressed as (surveyed - design) / design × 100. Enables normalised comparison across survey areas of different sizes for production scheduling KPI reporting.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Design Variance; JORC Code 2012

attributes.name: vertical_accuracy_m
attributes.description: Estimated vertical positional accuracy of the survey in metres (m), representing the RMSE of elevation check point comparisons. Critical for volumetric calculation reliability and bench floor compliance.

attributes.name: volume_change_m3
attributes.description: Net volumetric change in cubic metres (m³) between the current survey and the previous survey for the same location. Positive values indicate material addition (e.g., stockpile build); negative values indicate material removal (e.g., pit excavation, reclaim).
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Volume Reconciliation; JORC Code 2012

attributes.name: weather_conditions
attributes.description: Prevailing weather conditions at the time of the survey, which may affect data quality for drone photogrammetry and LiDAR methods. Used for data quality qualification and survey validity assessment.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan — Survey Quality Notes; ISO 19157

products.name: production_reconciliation
products.description: Periodic production reconciliation record comparing geological model predictions to actual mined tonnes and grades. Captures reconciliation period, ore source, model tonnes vs actual tonnes, model grade vs actual grade, reconciliation factor (F1/F2/F3), variance explanation, and sign-off. Sourced from LabWare LIMS, Caterpillar MineStar, and Geovia GEMS. Critical for JORC compliance and resource model confidence.

attributes.name: production_reconciliation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each production reconciliation record in the silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: block_model_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.block_model. Business justification: Reconciliation validates specific block model versions against actual mining results. Critical for model versioning, competent person reviews, and determining when model updates are required.

attributes.name: geological_domain_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.geological_domain. Business justification: Reconciliation is performed by geological domain to identify model biases. Required for domain-specific model updates, understanding estimation performance, and refining variogram parameters.

attributes.name: lom_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.lom_plan. Business justification: Reconciliation compares actuals to LOM plan predictions. N:1 relationship (many reconciliations reference one LOM plan). No bidirectional conflict. Valid planning link.

attributes.name: mine_site_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.mine_site. Business justification: production_reconciliation has mine_site_code (STRING) but no FK to mine_site table. Adding mine_site_id FK normalizes site reference and removes redundant code column. The mine_site table contains sit

attributes.name: mining_block_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.mining_block. Business justification: Reconciliation is performed at mining block level. N:1 relationship (many reconciliation records per block over time). No bidirectional conflict. Valid operational link.

attributes.name: ore_reserve_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.ore_reserve. Business justification: Reconciliation tracks reserve depletion. Reserve reconciliation is a regulatory requirement comparing mined tonnes against declared reserves for stock exchange reporting, reserve replacement tracking,

attributes.name: orebody_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.orebody. Business justification: Reconciliation compares model vs actual performance by orebody. Required for resource model updates, reserve confidence assessment, and identifying systematic geological estimation biases.

attributes.name: pit_design_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.pit_design. Business justification: Reconciliation can compare actuals to pit design. N:1 relationship (many reconciliations for one pit design). No bidirectional conflict. Valid planning link.

attributes.name: primary_production_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the qualified geologist responsible for preparing and validating the reconciliation record. The responsible geologist is a Competent Person under JORC or Qualified Person under NI 43-101 who certifies the geological model inputs.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Competent Person requirements; NI 43-101 Qualified Person; CIM

attributes.name: production_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.production_schedule. Business justification: Reconciliation compares actuals to a specific production schedule. N:1 relationship (many reconciliations can reference one schedule period). No bidirectional conflict. Valid operational link.

attributes.name: prospect_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.prospect. Business justification: Reconciliation compares actual production against exploration resource estimates at prospect level. Monthly/quarterly reconciliation is a regulatory requirement linking mined tonnes back to the origin

attributes.name: resource_estimate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.resource_estimate. Business justification: Reconciliation compares actual results against resource estimates. F1/F2/F3 factor calculation requires linking mined blocks to the source resource estimate for model updating, resource classification

attributes.name: resource_statement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.resource_statement. Business justification: Reconciliation validates resource statement accuracy over time. Required for material change assessments, determining when resource restatements are needed, and maintaining competent person confidence

attributes.name: stope_design_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.stope_design. Business justification: For underground mining reconciliation, linking to stope_design provides access to design parameters for comparison with actuals. This is essential for underground production reconciliation. No redunda

attributes.name: tenement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: Production reconciliation must track planned vs actual by tenement for reserve reporting updates, royalty calculation verification, and expenditure commitment substantiation. Required for annual reser

attributes.name: actual_grade
attributes.description: Actual head grade (percentage or grams per tonne) of the primary commodity as determined by assay results from LabWare LIMS for the reconciliation period. Used as the numerator in F2 (grade reconciliation factor) calculation.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Assay Results; JORC Code 2012; SAMREC Code 2016

attributes.name: actual_metal_content
attributes.description: Actual contained metal or mineral content (tonnes of metal) for the reconciliation period, derived from actual_tonnes and actual_grade assay data from LabWare LIMS. Used as the numerator in F3 (metal content reconciliation factor) calculation.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS; JORC Code 2012; SAMREC Code 2016

attributes.name: actual_tonnes
attributes.description: Actual ore tonnes mined and delivered to the ROM pad or processing plant during the reconciliation period, as measured by Caterpillar MineStar FMS payload data and survey. Used as the numerator in F1 (tonnes reconciliation factor) calculation.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Payload Management; JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards 2014

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the reconciliation record received final sign-off approval from the authorised approver. Null if reconciliation_status is not yet approved. Provides audit trail for JORC compliance and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; ISO 45001; SAP S/4HANA workflow

attributes.name: assay_sample_count
attributes.description: Number of assay samples collected and analysed in LabWare LIMS to determine the actual_grade for this reconciliation period. Higher sample counts increase grade confidence. Used to assess statistical reliability of the F2 grade reconciliation factor.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Sample Management; JORC Code 2012 Table 1

attributes.name: bench_elevation_m
attributes.description: Elevation in metres above sea level (mRL) of the mining bench or stope level from which the reconciled ore was extracted. Used to spatially locate the reconciliation within the mine design and correlate with the geological block model in Geovia GEMS.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS; Hexagon MinePlan Mine Design; GIS spatial reference

attributes.name: commodity_code
attributes.description: Standard code for the primary commodity being reconciled (e.g., FE for iron ore, CU for copper, LI for lithium, NI for nickel, COAL). Used to align reconciliation data with sales, trading, and JORC resource reporting.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards; London Metal Exchange commodity codes

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the production reconciliation record was first created in the system. Provides audit trail for data lineage and compliance with JORC documentation requirements.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; ISO 14001; GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement

attributes.name: dilution_pct
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of waste rock (gangue) mixed with ore during the mining process, contributing to grade reduction relative to the geological model. Calculated from blast movement monitoring and survey data. High dilution is a primary driver of negative F2 factors.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1; Caterpillar MineStar; Hexagon MinePlan

attributes.name: f1_factor
attributes.description: F1 reconciliation factor representing the ratio of actual mined tonnes to geological model tonnes (actual_tonnes / model_tonnes). A value of 1.0 indicates perfect tonnes reconciliation. Values significantly above or below 1.0 indicate geological model uncertainty or mining dilution issues. Critical JORC resource model confidence metric.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards 2014; Geovia GEMS Reconciliation

attributes.name: f2_factor
attributes.description: F2 reconciliation factor representing the ratio of actual mined grade to geological model grade (actual_grade / model_grade). A value of 1.0 indicates perfect grade reconciliation. Deviations indicate geological estimation error, sampling bias, or dilution effects. Critical for resource model confidence and JORC compliance.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; SAMREC Code 2016; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: f3_factor
attributes.description: F3 reconciliation factor representing the ratio of actual metal content to geological model metal content (actual_metal_content / model_metal_content). Combines the effect of both F1 and F2 (F3 = F1 × F2). The primary indicator of overall geological model performance and resource model confidence for JORC and NI 43-101 reporting.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101 Section 14; CIM Definition Standards 2014

attributes.name: grade_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for model_grade and actual_grade fields. Percentage (pct) is used for base metals such as copper and iron ore; grams per tonne (g_per_t) for gold and silver; parts per million (ppm) for trace elements.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; LabWare LIMS; SAMREC Code 2016

attributes.name: grade_variance_pct
attributes.description: Percentage variance between actual mined grade and geological model grade, expressed as ((actual_grade - model_grade) / model_grade) × 100. Positive values indicate higher-than-predicted grade; negative values indicate grade underperformance. Drives cut-off grade and ore/waste classification reviews.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; LabWare LIMS; Geovia GEMS

attributes.name: model_grade
attributes.description: Predicted head grade (percentage or grams per tonne) of the primary commodity for the reconciliation period as estimated in the geological block model. Used as the denominator in F2 (grade reconciliation factor) calculation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1; Geovia GEMS Resource Estimation; NI 43-101 Section 14

attributes.name: model_metal_content
attributes.description: Predicted contained metal or mineral content (tonnes of metal) for the reconciliation period, calculated as model_tonnes multiplied by model_grade. Represents the geological model's expected metal inventory. Used in F3 (metal content reconciliation factor) calculation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Geovia GEMS; NI 43-101 Section 14

attributes.name: model_tonnes
attributes.description: Predicted ore tonnes for the reconciliation period as derived from the geological block model in Geovia GEMS or Hexagon MinePlan. Represents the mine plan scheduled tonnes before actual mining. Used as the denominator in F1 (tonnes reconciliation factor) calculation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Geovia GEMS Block Model; NI 43-101 Section 14

attributes.name: model_update_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reconciliation results have triggered a requirement to update the geological block model in Geovia GEMS. Set to True when F1, F2, or F3 factors fall outside acceptable tolerance thresholds, indicating the resource model requires re-estimation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Geovia GEMS; NI 43-101 Section 14

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, caveats, or contextual information related to the reconciliation record that do not fit into structured fields. May include references to specific blast events, equipment downtime, or exceptional geological conditions observed during the period.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Geovia GEMS; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: ore_recovery_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of the geological model ore tonnes that were successfully extracted and delivered to the ROM pad or processing plant, accounting for ore losses to waste dumps or misclassification. Distinct from metallurgical recovery rate in the processing plant.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Geovia GEMS; Hexagon MinePlan

attributes.name: ore_source_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the specific ore source (e.g., pit bench, stope, ore block, or mining block) from which the reconciled tonnes were extracted. Sourced from Geovia GEMS block model and Hexagon MinePlan scheduling.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS Block Model; Hexagon MinePlan Scheduling; JORC Code 2012

attributes.name: ore_source_type
attributes.description: Classification of the ore source by mining method or material origin. Distinguishes between open-cut bench, underground stope, ROM pad stockpile, or blended feed to the processing plant. Critical for strip ratio and dilution analysis.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS; Hexagon MinePlan; JORC Code 2012 Table 1

attributes.name: period_type
attributes.description: Granularity of the reconciliation period. Determines the reporting cadence and is used to aggregate or disaggregate reconciliation factors (F1/F2/F3) for LOM planning and JORC resource model confidence assessments.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Geovia GEMS Reconciliation Module

attributes.name: reconciliation_period_end
attributes.description: End date of the production period covered by this reconciliation. Together with reconciliation_period_start defines the temporal scope of the comparison between geological model and actual production.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; IFRS 6 Exploration for and Evaluation of Mineral Resources

attributes.name: reconciliation_period_start
attributes.description: Start date of the production period covered by this reconciliation. Typically aligned to shift, daily, weekly, monthly, or quarterly reporting cycles.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; IFRS 6 Exploration for and Evaluation of Mineral Resources

attributes.name: reconciliation_reference
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the reconciliation run, typically formatted as REC-<SITE>-<YEAR>-<PERIOD>. Used for cross-system traceability across Geovia GEMS, LabWare LIMS, and Caterpillar MineStar.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1; Geovia GEMS Reconciliation Module

attributes.name: reconciliation_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the reconciliation record. Tracks progression from initial draft through geologist and mine manager review to final approval or rejection. Superseded indicates a newer reconciliation has replaced this record.

attributes.name: resource_classification
attributes.description: JORC resource or reserve classification of the ore source being reconciled. Measured and Proved Reserve classifications carry the highest geological confidence; Inferred carries the lowest. Reconciliation factors are tracked by classification to assess model confidence at each JORC category level. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: measured|indicated|inferred|proved_reserve|probable_reserve — promote to reference product if additional classifications such as SAMREC or NI 43-101 equivalents are required]
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC Code 2016; CIM Definition Standards 2014

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which the reconciliation data was primarily sourced. Geovia GEMS provides geological model data; Caterpillar MineStar provides actual tonnes via FMS; LabWare LIMS provides assay grade data. Manual indicates data was entered directly without system integration.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS; Caterpillar MineStar; LabWare LIMS; Hexagon MinePlan

attributes.name: survey_method
attributes.description: Method used to measure actual mined tonnes for the reconciliation period. Drone survey and laser scan provide volumetric measurements; GPS RTK and total station provide traditional survey data; truck payload uses Caterpillar MineStar FMS payload data. Affects accuracy confidence of actual_tonnes.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Payload Management; Hexagon MinePlan Survey

attributes.name: tonnes_variance_pct
attributes.description: Percentage variance between actual mined tonnes and geological model tonnes, expressed as ((actual_tonnes - model_tonnes) / model_tonnes) × 100. Positive values indicate over-mining relative to model; negative values indicate under-mining. Used for production scheduling variance reporting.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Hexagon MinePlan; Deswik Scheduling

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the production reconciliation record was most recently modified. Tracks revisions to reconciliation factors, variance explanations, or approval status. Essential for data lineage in the Databricks silver layer.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Databricks Delta Lake audit; ISO 14001

attributes.name: variance_category
attributes.description: Primary categorical classification of the reconciliation variance cause. Used for trend analysis and systematic identification of recurring model or operational issues. Supports resource model update prioritisation and mine planning improvement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: geological_model|dilution|ore_loss|sampling_bias|survey_error|blast_movement|equipment_error|classification_error — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Geovia GEMS; Hexagon MinePlan

attributes.name: variance_explanation
attributes.description: Narrative explanation of the primary causes of variance between geological model predictions and actual production results. Documents factors such as geological model uncertainty, blast movement, dilution, ore loss, sampling bias, or survey error. Required for JORC compliance documentation and resource model update decisions.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; SAMREC Code 2016; CIM Definition Standards 2014

products.name: equipment_schedule_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment of mining fleet and fixed plant assets to specific production schedules. It captures the planned deployment of equipment (haul trucks, excavators, drills, shovels, dozers, graders) to mining blocks, benches, and stopes for defined schedule periods. Each record links one production schedule to one asset with operational planning attributes including scheduled operating hours, utilisation targets, fuel budgets, and maintenance windows. This is the core of mine production planning and fleet deployment optimization, enabling mine planners to allocate equipment resources across multiple concurrent schedules and track asset utilisation across different mining areas and time periods.. Existence Justification: In mining operations, production schedules require multiple pieces of equipment (haul trucks, excavators, drills, dozers) to be deployed simultaneously to mining blocks and benches, and each asset works across multiple schedule periods and locations throughout the year. Mine planners actively create and manage these equipment assignments as part of the production planning workflow, tracking scheduled hours, utilisation targets, fuel budgets, and maintenance windows for each asset-schedule combination. This is a core operational business process called Equipment Scheduling or Fleet Assignment Planning.

attributes.name: equipment_schedule_assignment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each equipment schedule assignment record in the lakehouse

attributes.name: asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the specific mining asset (truck, excavator, drill, etc.) assigned to execute this production schedule

attributes.name: assigned_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the mine planner or production supervisor who created this equipment assignment. Used for accountability and assignment audit trail.

attributes.name: fleet_assignment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the equipment fleet or fleet configuration allocated to execute this production schedule. Links to the fleet management master record in Caterpillar MineStar FMS for execution tracking and OEE monitoring. [Moved from production_schedule: This attribute currently exists in production_schedule but represents the fleet configuration allocated to execute the schedule. In reality, equipment assignments are made at the individual asset level (not fleet level), and each asset assignment may have different parameters. If fleet_id is used for aggregate planning, it should remain in production_schedule as a planning input, but the actual asset-level assignments with their specific hours, utilisation, and fuel budgets belong in this association. However, upon review, equipment_fleet_id appears to be a fleet-level planning attribute (aggregate fleet configuration) rather than individual asset assignment data, so it should likely REMAIN in production_schedule as a planning input. Removing this from the move list.]
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar FMS; OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) Standard

attributes.name: production_schedule_id

attributes.name: assignment_created_timestamp

attributes.name: assignment_end_date

attributes.name: assignment_start_date

attributes.name: assignment_status

Values: 'planned' (assignment created but not yet active), 'active' (asset currently deployed to this schedule), 'completed' (schedule period finished), 'cancelled' (assignment removed before completion), 'suspended' (temporarily paused due to breakdown or reallocation). Used to track assignment lifecycle and enable dynamic fleet reallocation.

attributes.name: assignment_updated_timestamp

attributes.name: scheduled_maintenance_window

attributes.name: scheduled_operating_hours

attributes.name: scheduled_utilisation_pct

products.name: schedule_crew_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment of mine crews to production schedules. It captures the planned allocation of specific crews (drilling, blasting, loading, hauling, maintenance) to execute production schedules across different mining blocks, benches, and time periods. Each record links one production schedule to one crew with temporal and role-specific attributes that exist only in the context of this assignment relationship. Essential for workforce capacity planning, production schedule feasibility validation, and shift-based execution tracking.. Existence Justification: In mining operations, production schedules require multiple specialized crews to execute different phases of the extraction process - drilling crews prepare blast holes, blasting crews execute controlled explosions, loading crews operate excavators, and hauling crews transport material. Each crew is simultaneously assigned to multiple production schedules across different mining blocks, benches, and time periods based on equipment allocation, skill requirements, and operational sequencing. The assignment itself carries critical operational data including temporal coordination (scheduled start/end dates), role specification (what function the crew performs in this schedule), planned capacity (hours allocated), and status tracking (planned through completed).

products.name: stockpile_circuit_feed
products.description: This association product represents the operational feed scheduling relationship between ROM stockpiles and processing circuits. It captures the feed rate, blend ratio, and priority for each stockpile-circuit pairing, enabling mine-to-mill optimization and feed quality management. Each record links one ROM stockpile to one processing circuit with attributes that exist only in the context of this feed scheduling relationship.. Existence Justification: In mining operations, ROM stockpiles serve as intermediate storage between mining and processing, and the feed scheduling relationship is genuinely many-to-many. A single ROM stockpile can feed multiple processing circuits (e.g., high-grade material to primary circuit, low-grade to secondary circuit, oxide ore to leach circuit while sulphide goes to flotation). Conversely, a processing circuit draws from multiple stockpiles to achieve target feed grade through blending strategies. Plant metallurgists and production schedulers actively manage these feed relationships, adjusting blend ratios, feed rates, and priorities based on stockpile inventory, ore quality, and circuit performance.

attributes.name: conveyor_route_code

attributes.name: feed_status

attributes.name: reclaim_method
attributes.description: Method used to reclaim material from this stockpile for feeding this circuit (e.g., Front-End Loader, Reclaimer, Apron Feeder). Drives operational planning and equipment allocation.

attributes.name: reclaim_priority
attributes.description: Integer ranking indicating the priority order in which this stockpile should be reclaimed to the processing plant feed. Lower number = higher priority. Used by plant feed scheduling to manage blend quality and FIFO/grade-based reclaim strategies. [Moved from rom_stockpile: Reclaim priority is not an absolute property of the ROM stockpile itself, but rather depends on which circuit is being fed. A stockpile may have high priority for one circuit (e.g., oxide ore to leach circuit) but low priority for another (e.g., same stockpile to flotation circuit). This attribute belongs in the association as feed_priority.]

attributes.name: reclaim_rate_t_hr
attributes.description: Design or operational reclaim rate of material from this stockpile to the processing plant in tonnes per hour. Used for plant feed scheduling and production planning. [Moved from rom_stockpile: Reclaim rate varies by destination circuit based on circuit capacity, feed requirements, and blending strategy. A stockpile may feed different circuits at different rates. This attribute belongs in the association as feed_rate_tph.]

products.name: stockpile_blend
products.description: This association product represents the blending operation between ROM stockpiles and saleable products. It captures the operational reality that saleable products are created by blending material from multiple ROM stockpiles, and each ROM stockpile contributes to multiple saleable products. Each record links one ROM stockpile to one saleable product with blend ratios, quality contributions, reclaim sequences, and effective date ranges that exist only in the context of this blending relationship.. Existence Justification: In mining operations, saleable products are created by blending material from multiple ROM stockpiles to achieve target grade specifications, and each ROM stockpile contributes material to multiple different saleable products over time. Blending is an active operational process managed by mine planning and metallurgy teams who create blend recipes specifying which stockpiles to reclaim, in what sequence, at what ratios, to produce each product grade. This is a core operational M:N relationship with substantial relationship-specific data.

attributes.name: ore_grade_percent
attributes.description: Average ore grade of the primary commodity in this area, expressed as percentage.

attributes.name: ore_reserve_tonnes
attributes.description: Estimated proven and probable ore reserves in this area, measured in tonnes.

attributes.name: permit_expiry_date
attributes.description: Expiration date of the mining permit for this area.

attributes.name: permit_number
attributes.description: Regulatory permit or license number authorizing mining operations in this area.

attributes.name: production_capacity_tonnes_per_year
attributes.description: Designed annual production capacity of the mine area, measured in tonnes per year.

attributes.name: rehabilitation_status
attributes.description: Current status of mine closure and rehabilitation activities for the area.

attributes.name: responsible_superintendent
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the mining superintendent responsible for operations in this area.

attributes.name: scada_integration_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this area is integrated with SCADA systems for real-time operational monitoring.

attributes.name: shift_pattern
attributes.description: Operating shift pattern for this mine area, such as 24/7, day-shift-only, or FIFO roster pattern.

attributes.name: strip_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of waste material to ore that must be removed to extract the ore, expressed as waste:ore.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this mine area record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: water_management_zone
attributes.description: Designated water management zone or catchment area for environmental and operational water control.

attributes.name: parent_mine_area_id

products.name: blast_pattern
products.description: Master reference table for blast_pattern. Referenced by blast_pattern_id.

attributes.name: blast_pattern_id
attributes.description: Primary key for blast_pattern

attributes.name: approved_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the authorized person (typically a senior mining engineer or blasting superintendent) who approved this blast pattern for operational use.

attributes.name: designed_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the mining engineer or blast designer who created this blast pattern.

attributes.name: explosive_type_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary explosive product used in this blast pattern (e.g., ANFO, emulsion, heavy ANFO).

attributes.name: geological_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the geological rock type or lithology for which this blast pattern is optimized (e.g., iron ore, overburden, coal, hard rock).

attributes.name: mine_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the mine site where this blast pattern is designed for use.

attributes.name: pit_or_level_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific open-cut pit or mining area where this blast pattern is applied.

attributes.name: application_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing operational guidance, constraints, or special instructions for applying this blast pattern in the field.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the blast pattern was formally approved for operational use.

attributes.name: bench_height_m
attributes.description: Vertical height of the bench face in meters for which this blast pattern is designed. Critical parameter for calculating explosive load and fragmentation outcomes.

attributes.name: burden_m
attributes.description: Perpendicular distance in meters from the blast hole to the free face. Primary design parameter controlling rock movement and fragmentation.

attributes.name: charge_length_m
attributes.description: Total length of the explosive column in meters within the blast hole.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this blast pattern record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: delay_timing_ms
attributes.description: Time delay in milliseconds between detonation of adjacent blast holes, used to control vibration, fragmentation, and muck pile throw.

attributes.name: design_date
attributes.description: Date when the blast pattern was originally designed.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this blast pattern becomes valid for operational use.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date until which this blast pattern remains valid. Nullable for patterns with indefinite validity.

attributes.name: explosive_mass_per_hole_kg
attributes.description: Total mass of explosive loaded into each blast hole in kilograms.

attributes.name: fragmentation_target_p80_mm
attributes.description: Target fragmentation size in millimeters where 80% of the blasted material passes through (P80 metric). Drives crusher feed requirements and downstream processing efficiency.

attributes.name: hole_depth_m
attributes.description: Total depth of the blast hole in meters, including sub-drill below the bench floor to ensure complete breakage.

attributes.name: hole_diameter_mm
attributes.description: Diameter of the blast holes in millimeters. Determines explosive charge capacity and influences fragmentation and powder factor.

attributes.name: initiation_system_type
attributes.description: Type of detonation initiation system used in the blast pattern. Electronic systems offer precise timing; non-electric and shock tube systems are cost-effective alternatives.

attributes.name: is_standard_pattern
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is a standard, repeatable blast pattern (true) or a custom, one-off design (false).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this blast pattern record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: number_of_holes
attributes.description: Total count of blast holes in the pattern design.

attributes.name: number_of_rows
attributes.description: Number of rows of blast holes in the pattern, measured perpendicular to the free face.

attributes.name: pattern_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique code identifying the blast pattern design, used in operational communications and drill-and-blast planning systems.

attributes.name: pattern_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation of the blast pattern, typically describing the geometry or application context.

attributes.name: pattern_type
attributes.description: Classification of the blast pattern geometry. Square and rectangular patterns are common in open-cut operations; staggered patterns optimize energy distribution; echelon patterns suit angled benches; radial patterns are used in underground or specialized applications.

attributes.name: powder_factor_kg_per_m3
attributes.description: Mass of explosive in kilograms required to break one cubic meter of rock. Key performance indicator for blast efficiency and cost control.

attributes.name: rock_strength_mpa
attributes.description: Unconfined compressive strength of the target rock in megapascals. Influences explosive selection and powder factor requirements.

attributes.name: safety_exclusion_zone_m
attributes.description: Minimum safe distance in meters from the blast area within which all personnel and equipment must be evacuated prior to detonation.

attributes.name: spacing_m
attributes.description: Distance in meters between adjacent blast holes in the same row. Typically 1.0 to 1.5 times the burden distance.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the blast pattern. Active patterns are approved for operational use; draft patterns are under design; retired patterns are no longer used but retained for historical reference.

attributes.name: stemming_length_m
attributes.description: Length of inert material (typically crushed rock or drill cuttings) placed at the top of the blast hole in meters to confine explosive gases and prevent premature venting.

attributes.name: sub_drill_m
attributes.description: Additional drilling depth below the bench floor in meters to ensure complete rock breakage at the toe of the blast.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of the blast pattern design, incremented when modifications are made to an existing pattern.

attributes.name: adjacent_blast_pattern_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on blast_pattern (adjacent_blast_pattern_id)

products.name: pit_or_level
products.description: Master reference table for pit_or_level. Referenced by pit_or_level_id.

attributes.name: pit_or_level_id
attributes.description: Primary key for pit_or_level

attributes.name: mine_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent mine site where this pit or level is located.

attributes.name: rehabilitation_provision_id
attributes.description: Reference to the approved environmental rehabilitation plan for this pit or level upon closure.

attributes.name: access_ramp_code
attributes.description: Reference to the primary access ramp or decline providing haulage access to this pit or level.

attributes.name: actual_completion_date
attributes.description: Actual date when mining operations were completed at this pit or level. Used for historical analysis and future planning accuracy.

attributes.name: actual_start_date
attributes.description: Actual date when mining operations commenced at this pit or level. Used for schedule variance analysis and performance tracking.

attributes.name: average_ore_grade_percent
attributes.description: Average grade of ore at this pit or level, expressed as percentage of target mineral content. Business-sensitive data used for mine sequencing and blending strategies.

attributes.name: bench_height_m
attributes.description: Vertical height of the mining bench at this level, measured in meters. Standard bench heights are critical for blast design and equipment selection.

attributes.name: blast_pattern_code
attributes.description: Standard blast design pattern code used at this pit or level. References drill spacing, burden, and explosive configuration for this geological domain.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pit or level record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit purposes.

attributes.name: cutoff_grade_percent
attributes.description: Minimum ore grade threshold for economic extraction at this pit or level, expressed as percentage. Material below this grade is classified as waste.

attributes.name: depth_m
attributes.description: Vertical depth of the pit or level from surface or reference datum, measured in meters. Used for geotechnical analysis and ventilation planning.

attributes.name: design_capacity_tonnes_per_day
attributes.description: Planned daily production capacity for this pit or level, measured in tonnes per day. Used for production scheduling and resource allocation.

attributes.name: dilution_factor_percent
attributes.description: Expected percentage of waste material mixed with ore during extraction at this pit or level. Used for grade reconciliation and mill feed planning.

attributes.name: elevation_m
attributes.description: Elevation of the pit floor or level datum above sea level, measured in meters. Critical for mine planning, haulage optimization, and surveying.

attributes.name: geotechnical_risk_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of ground stability and geotechnical hazards at this pit or level: low (stable), moderate (manageable risks), high (significant controls required), or extreme (critical hazard management).

attributes.name: haulage_distance_km
attributes.description: Average haulage distance from this pit or level to the primary destination (ROM pad, crusher, or waste dump), measured in kilometers. Used for cycle time and cost modeling.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this pit or level record is currently active and valid for operational use. True indicates active, False indicates inactive or archived.

attributes.name: mining_method
attributes.description: The extraction method employed at this pit or level: open-cut/open-pit for surface mining, underground methods including block cave, sublevel stoping, longwall, or room and pillar.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the pit or level for identification and communication purposes.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special conditions, or additional context about this pit or level.

attributes.name: ore_reserve_tonnes
attributes.description: Estimated economically recoverable ore reserves at this pit or level, measured in tonnes. Business-sensitive reserve data used for Life of Mine (LOM) planning.

attributes.name: pit_or_level_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the pit or level, used in operational systems and reporting. Externally-known unique code.

attributes.name: planned_completion_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for completion of mining operations at this pit or level. Used for Life of Mine (LOM) planning and closure planning.

attributes.name: planned_start_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for commencement of mining operations at this pit or level. Used for production scheduling and resource planning.

attributes.name: primary_commodity
attributes.description: The primary mineral commodity being extracted from this pit or level: iron ore, copper, coal, lithium, nickel, gold, silver, zinc, lead, or bauxite.

attributes.name: recovery_factor_percent
attributes.description: Expected percentage of in-situ ore that will be successfully extracted and recovered from this pit or level. Accounts for mining losses and operational constraints.

attributes.name: secondary_commodity
attributes.description: Secondary or by-product mineral commodity present at this pit or level, if applicable. Used for polymetallic deposit planning and revenue optimization.

attributes.name: slope_angle_degrees
attributes.description: Design slope angle for pit walls or level access at this location, measured in degrees from horizontal. Critical for geotechnical stability and safety.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the pit or level: planned (future), design (engineering phase), development (construction), active (in production), depleted (ore exhausted), suspended (temporarily halted), closed (operations ceased), or rehabilitated (environmental restoration complete).

attributes.name: strip_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of waste to ore for this pit or level, calculated as waste volume divided by ore volume. Key economic indicator for open-cut mining operations.

attributes.name: surveyed_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent survey measurement for this pit or level. Used for as-built reconciliation and spatial accuracy tracking.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Classification of the mining excavation structure: pit for open-cut operations, level for underground operations, bench for stepped excavation, stage for phased development, cutback for pit expansion, or pushback for sequential mining phases.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pit or level record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: ventilation_requirement_m3_per_sec
attributes.description: Required airflow rate for underground levels, measured in cubic meters per second. Critical for occupational health and safety compliance.

attributes.name: waste_volume_bcm
attributes.description: Estimated volume of waste material to be removed from this pit or level, measured in bank cubic meters. Critical for strip ratio calculation and waste dump planning.

attributes.name: water_inflow_rate_liters_per_min
attributes.business_glossary_term: Water Inflow Rate Liters Per Min
attributes.description: Average groundwater inflow rate at this pit or level, measured in liters per minute. Used for dewatering system design and water management planning.

attributes.name: parent_pit_or_level_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on pit_or_level (parent_pit_or_level_id)

products.name: bench

attributes.name: mine_site_id

attributes.name: bench_name

attributes.name: bench_status

attributes.name: bench_type
attributes.description: Classification of the bench based on material type: ore-bearing, waste rock, mixed material, overburden, or interburden.

attributes.name: bench_width_m
attributes.description: Horizontal width of the bench working area in meters, measured from crest to toe.

attributes.name: berm_width_m
attributes.description: Width of the safety berm or catch bench in meters, designed to catch falling material and provide access.

attributes.name: blast_pattern_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the standard drill-and-blast pattern design used for this bench.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: design_capacity_bcm

attributes.name: drill_hole_burden_m
attributes.description: Standard distance from the drill hole to the free face (burden) in the blast pattern, measured in meters.

attributes.name: drill_hole_diameter_mm

attributes.name: drill_hole_spacing_m

attributes.name: elevation_rl_m
attributes.description: The reduced level elevation of the bench floor in meters above mean sea level, used for vertical positioning in mine design.

attributes.name: face_angle_degrees
attributes.description: Angle of the bench face in degrees from horizontal, critical for geotechnical stability and safety.

attributes.name: geotechnical_domain
attributes.description: Geotechnical classification or domain code for the bench, indicating rock mass characteristics and stability parameters.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the bench is currently active in production operations.

attributes.name: material_type
attributes.description: Primary geological material type present in the bench (e.g., iron ore, copper ore, coal, limestone, sandstone).

attributes.name: mining_method
attributes.description: Primary extraction method used for the bench: drill-and-blast, rip-and-load (dozer ripping), direct loading, or selective mining.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, comments, or special instructions related to the bench.

attributes.name: ore_grade_percent
attributes.description: Average ore grade percentage for the bench, representing the concentration of valuable mineral content.

attributes.name: ore_tonnes
attributes.description: Estimated total tonnage of ore material within the bench.

attributes.name: phase_code
attributes.description: Mine planning phase code indicating which development phase or pushback this bench belongs to.

attributes.name: planned_completion_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date when mining operations are planned to be completed on this bench, per the Life of Mine (LOM) plan.

attributes.name: planned_start_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date when mining operations are planned to commence on this bench, per the Life of Mine (LOM) plan.

attributes.name: remaining_volume_bcm
attributes.description: Current remaining volume of material available for extraction from the bench in bank cubic meters.

attributes.name: rock_mass_rating
attributes.description: Rock Mass Rating score for the bench, a geotechnical classification system indicating rock quality and stability.

attributes.name: sequence_number
attributes.description: Mining sequence order number for the bench within the pit development plan, indicating the planned extraction order.

attributes.name: strip_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of waste tonnes to ore tonnes for the bench, a key economic indicator for mining operations.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the bench record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: waste_tonnes
attributes.description: Estimated total tonnage of waste material within the bench.

attributes.name: parent_bench_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on bench (parent_bench_id)

attributes.name: access_restriction

attributes.name: active_flag

attributes.name: actual_end_date
attributes.description: Actual date when operations ceased at this location. Nullable for active locations.

attributes.name: actual_start_date
attributes.description: Actual date when operations commenced at this location.

attributes.name: area_sqm
attributes.description: Surface area of the location in square meters. Used for capacity planning, rehabilitation costing, and environmental impact assessment.

attributes.name: bench_height_m
attributes.description: Vertical height of mining benches at this location in meters. Applicable to open-cut operations.

attributes.name: blast_zone_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the location is within an active blast zone requiring special safety protocols.

attributes.name: capacity_tonnes
attributes.description: Maximum material capacity of the location in tonnes. Used for stockpile management, ROM pad planning, and dump scheduling.

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: Spatial reference system used for location coordinates (e.g., WGS84, UTM Zone 50S, MGA94 Zone 51).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this location record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the location including operational context, boundaries, and special characteristics.

attributes.name: drainage_zone
attributes.description: Water drainage zone or catchment area identifier for the location. Used for water management and environmental compliance.

attributes.name: elevation_m
attributes.description: Elevation of the location above mean sea level in meters. Critical for pit design, haul road planning, and drainage management.

attributes.name: environmental_zone
attributes.description: Environmental management zone classification for the location (e.g., rehabilitation zone, buffer zone, heritage area).

attributes.name: geotechnical_risk_rating

attributes.name: grade_percent

attributes.name: haul_distance_km
attributes.description: Average haul distance from this location to the primary destination (e.g., crusher, ROM pad, waste dump) in kilometers.

attributes.name: last_survey_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent survey or measurement of this location. Critical for maintaining accurate spatial data and volume calculations.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the location centroid in decimal degrees (WGS84).

attributes.name: location_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique code for the location used across operational systems and reporting.

attributes.name: location_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the location (e.g., pit name, dump name, stockpile name, ROM pad identifier).

attributes.name: location_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the location in its lifecycle.

attributes.name: location_type
attributes.description: Classification of the location within the mining operation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pit|dump|stockpile|rom_pad|crusher|processing_plant|workshop|office|haul_road|bench|ramp|portal|stope|drive|shaft|decline|ore_pass|waste_dump|tailings_storage_facility — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: longitude

attributes.name: mine_site_id

attributes.name: mining_method

attributes.name: ore_type

products.name: explosive_type
products.description: Master reference table for explosive_type. Referenced by explosive_type_id.

attributes.name: explosive_type_id
attributes.description: Primary key for explosive_type

attributes.name: application_type
attributes.description: Primary mining application context for this explosive type (surface, underground, both). Determines operational suitability.

attributes.name: approval_authority
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory body or authority that has approved this explosive type for use (e.g., state mining department, federal agency).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which regulatory approval was granted for this explosive type. Used for compliance tracking and audit purposes.

attributes.name: approval_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current regulatory approval expires and requires renewal. Null if approval does not expire.

attributes.name: classification
attributes.description: Primary classification category of the explosive based on form and composition (bulk, packaged, emulsion, ANFO, watergel, slurry).

attributes.name: code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code used to identify the explosive type in operational systems and blast designs. Typically 2-10 characters.

attributes.name: compatibility_group
attributes.description: Single letter (A-S) indicating which explosives can be stored and transported together based on hazard compatibility.

attributes.name: cost_per_kg
attributes.description: Standard cost per kilogram of this explosive type in the base currency. Used for blast cost estimation and budgeting.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this explosive type record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the cost_per_kg field (e.g., USD, AUD, CAD).

attributes.name: density_kg_per_m3
attributes.description: Typical density of the explosive in kilograms per cubic meter. Critical for blast design calculations and loading specifications.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the explosive type including composition, characteristics, and typical use cases in mining operations.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this explosive type record became effective and available for operational use.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date on which this explosive type record ceased to be effective. Null if currently effective.

attributes.name: energy_content_mj_per_kg
attributes.description: Energy released per kilogram of explosive, measured in megajoules. Used for blast energy calculations and fragmentation modeling.

attributes.name: fume_class
attributes.description: Classification of toxic fume production (Class 1 = lowest toxicity, Class 3 = highest). Important for underground operations and ventilation planning.

attributes.name: hazard_class
attributes.description: Dangerous goods hazard class and division for the explosive (e.g., 1.1, 1.5) per international transport regulations.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Indicates whether this explosive type is currently active and available for use in blast designs. True = active, False = inactive/discontinued.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this explosive type record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary manufacturer or supplier of this explosive type. Used for procurement and quality assurance.

attributes.name: minimum_priming_requirement
attributes.description: Minimum primer or booster size and type required to reliably initiate this explosive type. Critical for blast design and safety.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Full commercial or technical name of the explosive type (e.g., ANFO, Emulsion, Heavy ANFO, Bulk Emulsion).

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or special instructions related to this explosive type. Free-text field for operational guidance.

attributes.name: product_family
attributes.description: Manufacturer's product family or series name to which this explosive type belongs. Groups related explosive products.

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_status
attributes.description: Current regulatory approval status for use in mining operations (approved, pending, expired, suspended, withdrawn).

attributes.name: relative_bulk_strength_percent
attributes.description: Explosive strength per unit volume relative to ANFO. Accounts for density differences in blast design calculations.

attributes.name: relative_weight_strength_percent
attributes.description: Explosive strength relative to ANFO (100%). Used to calculate equivalent explosive quantities and blast design parameters.

attributes.name: sensitivity_rating
attributes.description: Sensitivity of the explosive to initiation by impact, friction, or heat (very_low, low, moderate, high, very_high). Affects handling and storage requirements.

attributes.name: shelf_life_months
attributes.description: Maximum storage duration in months before the explosive degrades or requires re-certification. Used for inventory management and rotation.

attributes.name: temperature_range_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum ambient temperature in Celsius at which the explosive maintains reliable performance and safety characteristics.

attributes.name: temperature_range_min_c
attributes.description: Minimum ambient temperature in Celsius at which the explosive maintains reliable performance and safety characteristics.

attributes.name: typical_hole_diameter_max_mm
attributes.description: Maximum blast hole diameter in millimeters for which this explosive type is typically suitable. Guides blast design parameters.

attributes.name: typical_hole_diameter_min_mm
attributes.description: Minimum blast hole diameter in millimeters for which this explosive type is typically suitable. Guides blast design parameters.

attributes.name: un_number
attributes.description: Four-digit UN identification number for the explosive type used in transportation and regulatory compliance (e.g., UN0082, UN0241).

attributes.name: velocity_of_detonation_m_per_s
attributes.business_glossary_term: Velocity Of Detonation M Per S
attributes.description: Speed at which the detonation wave travels through the explosive, measured in meters per second. Key performance indicator for explosive effectiveness.

attributes.name: water_resistance
attributes.description: Ability of the explosive to maintain performance in wet conditions (none, poor, fair, good, excellent). Critical for wet hole applications.

attributes.name: parent_explosive_type_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on explosive_type (parent_explosive_type_id)

attributes.description: Primary key for access_ramp

attributes.description: Date when construction of the access ramp was completed and the ramp was ready for commissioning.

attributes.name: design_capacity_tonnes_per_hour

attributes.name: drainage_system_installed

attributes.name: emergency_egress_route

attributes.name: geotechnical_rating

attributes.name: gradient_percent

attributes.name: ground_support_type
attributes.description: Type of ground support system installed to maintain ramp stability and prevent rock falls.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent safety and structural inspection of the ramp.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp

attributes.name: length_meters
attributes.description: Total length of the access ramp in meters from entry to exit point.

attributes.name: lighting_installed

attributes.name: maximum_vehicle_weight_tonnes
attributes.description: Maximum gross vehicle weight in tonnes permitted to use this ramp based on structural and geotechnical design limits.

attributes.name: mine_site_id

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date

attributes.name: ore_type_access

attributes.name: pit_id

attributes.name: ramp_name

attributes.name: ramp_status

attributes.name: ramp_type

attributes.name: remarks

attributes.name: speed_limit_kmh

attributes.name: surface_type

attributes.name: traffic_direction
attributes.description: Permitted traffic flow direction on the ramp for operational safety and efficiency.

attributes.name: ventilation_type
attributes.description: Type of ventilation system installed in the ramp for air quality and safety management, particularly relevant for underground ramps.

attributes.name: vertical_depth_meters
attributes.description: The vertical distance in meters that the ramp descends or ascends, representing the elevation change from surface or reference level.

attributes.name: width_meters
