attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tailings.tsf. Business justification: Dense media separation rejects (float_tonnes_dry) sent to specific TSF. Operational necessity for material tracking, TSF capacity planning, and mass balance. Tracks DMS tailings stream destination.

attributes.name: circuit_availability_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of the scheduled operating time during which the DMS circuit was available and operational during this event period. Calculated as (operating hours / scheduled hours) × 100. Key input to Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) reporting.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Asset Availability Reporting; Internal OEE Standard

attributes.name: circuit_recovery_pct
attributes.description: Metallurgical recovery rate of the DMS circuit for this event, expressed as the percentage of valuable mineral in the feed that is recovered in the product stream. Core KPI for DMS circuit performance against LOM plan targets.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 — Recovery Rate Reporting; ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Framework

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this DMS event record was first created in the system, providing audit trail for data lineage and compliance purposes.

attributes.name: cyclone_pressure_kpa
attributes.description: Operating pressure of the DMS cyclone(s) measured in kilopascals (kPa) during this event. Cyclone pressure directly affects separation efficiency and is a key SCADA-monitored process control parameter.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System — SCADA Integration; P&ID Operating Standard

attributes.name: downtime_duration_min
attributes.description: Total duration of unplanned and planned downtime experienced by the DMS circuit during this event, measured in minutes. Used for availability calculations, maintenance planning, and OPEX impact assessment.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Work Order Management; Internal Downtime Reporting Standard

attributes.name: downtime_reason
attributes.description: Description of the primary cause of DMS circuit downtime during this event (e.g., cyclone blockage, pump failure, medium drain, planned maintenance, feed interruption). Used for root cause analysis and maintenance planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: cyclone_blockage|pump_failure|medium_drain|planned_maintenance|feed_interruption|screen_blinding|magnetic_drum_fault|electrical_fault — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Failure Code Register; Internal Downtime Classification Standard

attributes.name: event_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the DMS circuit operational event concluded. Used with start timestamp to calculate shift duration and throughput metrics.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System — Process Data Historian

attributes.name: event_number
attributes.description: Business-facing externally-known reference number for the DMS shift event, used for cross-system traceability and operational reporting. Format: DMS-YYYY-MM-DD-NNNN.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System — Event Frame Reference

attributes.name: event_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the DMS circuit operational event commenced, representing the principal real-world business event time. Sourced from OSIsoft PI System SCADA integration.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System — Process Data Historian

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the DMS event record, tracking progression from data capture through metallurgist review and sign-off to final closure.

attributes.name: feed_moisture_pct
attributes.description: Moisture content of the ore feed expressed as a percentage of wet weight. Critical for converting wet tonnes to dry metric tonnes (DMT) for metallurgical accounting and product quality reporting.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS — Sample Analysis; ISO 589 (Coal Moisture Determination)

attributes.name: feed_particle_size_p80_mm
attributes.description: 80th percentile particle size of the DMS feed in millimetres, representing the size at which 80% of feed particles pass. Influences separation efficiency and medium stability in the DMS circuit.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS — Particle Size Analysis; Internal Comminution Standard

attributes.name: feed_rate_target_tph
attributes.description: Planned feed rate target for the DMS circuit in tonnes per hour (tph) for this event period, sourced from the production schedule or LOM plan. Enables throughput variance analysis against actual feed_rate_tph.
attributes.references: Deswik — Production Scheduling; Hexagon MinePlan; Internal Throughput KPI Standard

attributes.name: feed_rate_tph
attributes.description: Mass flow rate of Run of Mine (ROM) ore fed into the DMS circuit during this event, measured in tonnes per hour (tph). Key throughput metric benchmarked against design capacity and LOM plan targets.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System — Process Data Historian; Internal Throughput KPI Standard

attributes.name: feed_tonnes_wet
attributes.description: Total wet mass of ore fed into the DMS circuit during the event period, measured in wet metric tonnes. Used for mass balance calculations and shift production reconciliation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 — Mass Balance; Internal Metallurgical Accounting Standard

attributes.name: float_tonnes_dry
attributes.description: Total dry metric tonnes (DMT) of material reporting to the float stream during this DMS event. Used for mass balance closure, metallurgical accounting, and clean product inventory tracking.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 — Mass Balance; Internal Metallurgical Accounting Standard

attributes.name: float_yield_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of the DMS feed that reports to the float (light) product stream, expressed as a mass percentage. For coal DMS, the float is the clean coal product; for iron ore, the float is typically the gangue reject.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 — Yield Reporting; Internal Metallurgical Accounting Standard

attributes.name: magnetic_recovery_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of dense medium (ferrosilicon or magnetite) recovered from the product and reject streams via magnetic drum separators during this event. High magnetic recovery reduces medium losses and OPEX. Benchmarked against circuit design targets.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System — SCADA Integration; Internal Medium Recovery SOP

attributes.name: medium_density_sg
attributes.description: Specific gravity (SG) of the dense medium (typically ferrosilicon or magnetite suspension) used in the DMS circuit during this event. The primary separation control parameter — particles denser than the medium sink, lighter particles float.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System — SCADA Integration; Internal DMS Operating Standard

attributes.name: medium_loss_kg_per_t
attributes.description: Mass of dense medium (ferrosilicon or magnetite) lost per tonne of feed processed during this DMS event, measured in kg/t. Medium losses are a significant operating cost driver and are tracked for reagent consumption reporting and OPEX management.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO — Cost Management; Internal OPEX Reporting Standard

attributes.name: medium_to_ore_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of dense medium volume to ore feed volume in the DMS circuit during this event. A key process control parameter affecting separation efficiency and medium stability. Typically expressed as m³ medium per tonne of ore.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System — Process Data Historian; Internal DMS SOP

attributes.name: medium_type
attributes.description: Type of dense medium used in the DMS circuit. Ferrosilicon is used for higher-density separations (diamonds, iron ore), while magnetite is common for coal DMS circuits. Affects reagent cost and medium recovery efficiency.

attributes.name: ore_type
attributes.description: Geological classification of the ore feed processed during this DMS event (e.g., oxide, sulphide, transitional, ROM blend). Influences medium density settings and expected sink/float yields. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oxide|sulphide|transitional|rom_blend|high_ash|low_ash|coking|thermal — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 — Ore Type Classification; Geovia GEMS

attributes.name: product_grade_pct
attributes.description: Grade of the valuable mineral in the DMS product stream, expressed as a percentage. For coal, this is ash content of clean coal; for iron ore, this is Fe%; for diamonds, this is carats per hundred tonnes (cpht). Benchmarked against LOM plan targets.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 — Grade Reporting; LabWare LIMS — Assay Results

attributes.name: production_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which this DMS event occurred, used for daily production reporting, metallurgical balance reconciliation, and LOM plan variance tracking.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Internal Production Reporting Standard

attributes.name: recovery_target_pct
attributes.description: Planned metallurgical recovery rate target for the DMS circuit during this event period, sourced from the LOM plan or shift production plan. Enables real-time variance tracking against actual circuit_recovery_pct.
attributes.references: Deswik — Mine Scheduling; Hexagon MinePlan; JORC Code 2012

attributes.name: reject_grade_pct
attributes.description: Grade of the valuable mineral in the DMS reject (discard) stream, expressed as a percentage. Used to assess mineral losses to tailings and validate separation efficiency. High reject grade indicates potential recovery improvement opportunity.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 — Grade Reporting; LabWare LIMS — Assay Results

attributes.name: shift_type
attributes.description: Classification of the shift period during which the DMS event occurred (day, afternoon, or night). Used for shift-comparative performance analysis and crew scheduling.

attributes.name: sink_tonnes_dry
attributes.description: Total dry metric tonnes (DMT) of material reporting to the sink stream during this DMS event. Used for mass balance closure, metallurgical accounting, and product inventory reconciliation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 — Mass Balance; Internal Metallurgical Accounting Standard

attributes.name: sink_yield_pct

attributes.name: maintenance_work_order_id

attributes.name: shift_production_run_id

attributes.name: shift_report_id

attributes.name: actual_value

attributes.name: alarm_tag

attributes.name: circuit_stage

attributes.name: corrective_action

attributes.name: corrective_action_type

attributes.name: deviation_magnitude

attributes.name: deviation_number

attributes.name: deviation_pct

attributes.name: deviation_status

attributes.name: duration_mins

attributes.name: escalation_flag

attributes.name: parameter_name

attributes.name: resolved_timestamp

attributes.name: root_cause_category

products.name: circuit_analytical_protocol
products.description: This association product represents the approved analytical method assignment between processing circuits and laboratory analytical methods. It captures the operational protocol governing which analytical methods are approved for use on each circuit's samples, including method priority, turnaround requirements, cost allocation, and QAQC insertion rates. Each record links one processing circuit to one analytical method with attributes that exist only in the context of this circuit-method relationship.. Existence Justification: In mining operations, processing circuits require multiple analytical methods to characterize feed, intermediate streams, and final products - a flotation circuit may use XRF for rapid grade control, ICP-MS for trace element monitoring, and fire assay for precious metal accountability. Conversely, each analytical method (e.g., XRF pressed pellet) is approved for use across multiple circuits with circuit-specific protocols governing turnaround time, sampling frequency, QAQC insertion rates, and cost allocation. The business actively manages these circuit-method protocols as operational entities.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the approved analytical method used for this circuit

attributes.description: Name or identifier of the technical authority (metallurgist, process engineer, or laboratory manager) who approved this method for this circuit

attributes.name: cost_allocation_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of this circuit's analytical budget allocated to this specific method, used for cost tracking and budget forecasting

attributes.description: Date from which this circuit-method protocol became active and operational

attributes.description: Date on which this circuit-method protocol was superseded or retired. Null for currently active protocols.

products.name: circuit_asset_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the Assignment between processing_circuit and asset. It captures the operational assignment of physical equipment assets to processing circuits within mineral processing plants, including duty classification, installation lifecycle dates, and performance contribution tracking. Each record links one processing_circuit to one asset with attributes that exist only in the context of this assignment relationship.. Existence Justification: In mining processing operations, circuits contain multiple physical assets (mills, pumps, cyclones, flotation cells, conveyors) that work together to process ore through a specific metallurgical process. Individual assets can be reassigned between circuits during plant reconfigurations, capacity expansions, or when equipment is moved from one circuit to another for operational optimization. The business actively manages these assignments with specific installation/removal dates, duty classifications (primary/standby), circuit positions, and tracks performance contribution for metallurgical accounting.

attributes.name: circuit_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Circuit Asset Assignment - Processing Circuit Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the processing circuit to which the asset is assigned

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the assignment indicating whether the asset is actively operating in the circuit, temporarily inactive, under maintenance, or being reconfigured.

attributes.name: circuit_position
attributes.description: Specific position or location code of the asset within the circuit flowsheet (e.g., PRIMARY_MILL_1, ROUGHER_CELL_3, CYCLONE_BANK_A). Used for circuit configuration management and maintenance work order routing.

attributes.name: duty_classification
attributes.description: Operational duty classification of the asset within the circuit indicating whether it operates as primary equipment, secondary/parallel unit, or standby/backup capacity. Drives maintenance prioritization and availability calculations.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the asset was physically installed and commissioned into the processing circuit. Used for asset lifecycle tracking and performance period calculation.

attributes.name: operating_hours
attributes.description: Cumulative operating hours logged by the asset while assigned to this specific circuit. Used for circuit-specific maintenance scheduling and performance analysis. Distinct from the asset's total SMR hours across all assignments.

attributes.name: performance_contribution_pct
attributes.description: Percentage contribution of this asset to the overall circuit throughput or recovery performance. Used for metallurgical accounting, bottleneck analysis, and asset performance attribution in multi-unit circuits.

attributes.name: removal_date
attributes.description: Date on which the asset was removed from the processing circuit due to maintenance, reconfiguration, or decommissioning. Null indicates the asset is currently assigned.

products.name: circuit_tailings_routing
products.description: This association product represents the operational routing configuration between processing circuits and Tailings Storage Facilities (TSFs). It captures the business rules and parameters governing where each circuit's tailings stream is directed, including geochemical routing decisions (e.g., acid-generating vs benign tailings), capacity-based routing, and time-based routing changes. Each record links one processing circuit to one TSF with routing-specific attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship. Critical for tailings management compliance, TSF capacity planning, and environmental risk management.. Existence Justification: In mining operations, processing circuits can route tailings to multiple TSFs based on geochemical properties (acid-generating vs benign), operational capacity constraints, and time-based transitions as facilities reach capacity or new TSFs are commissioned. Conversely, a single TSF receives tailings from multiple processing circuits (rougher, scavenger, cleaner circuits may all route to the same facility). The business actively manages these routing configurations with specific rules, priorities, and effective dates.

attributes.name: circuit_tailings_routing_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for this circuit-to-TSF routing configuration record

attributes.name: circuit_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Circuit Tailings Routing - Processing Circuit Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the processing circuit that generates the tailings stream

attributes.name: pipeline_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the physical tailings pipeline infrastructure used for this circuit-to-TSF routing. Links routing configuration to physical asset register.

attributes.name: tsf_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the Tailings Storage Facility receiving the tailings stream

attributes.name: design_slurry_density_pct
attributes.description: Target slurry density for this specific circuit-to-TSF routing expressed as percentage solids by weight. May differ from circuit design density based on TSF deposition requirements and water recovery strategies.

attributes.name: design_solids_rate_tph
attributes.description: Design basis dry solids flow rate from this circuit to this TSF expressed in tonnes per hour (tph). Used for TSF capacity planning and deposition rate modeling.

attributes.name: design_water_recovery_pct
attributes.description: Target percentage of process water to be recovered from this tailings stream at the receiving TSF. Varies by TSF design (thickened tailings, paste, conventional) and water balance strategy.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this circuit-to-TSF routing configuration became or will become active. Supports time-based routing changes as TSFs reach capacity or new facilities are commissioned.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date on which this circuit-to-TSF routing configuration ceased or will cease to be active. Null for currently active routings. Enables historical tracking of routing changes over mine life.

attributes.name: geochemical_routing_rule
attributes.description: Business rule describing the geochemical criteria governing this routing decision (e.g., 'ARD-generating tailings from copper rougher circuit routed to lined TSF-3', 'Benign tailings from final cleaner routed to unlined TSF-1'). Critical for environmental compliance and acid rock drainage management.

attributes.name: routing_priority
attributes.description: Integer priority ranking for this routing configuration when multiple TSF destinations are available for a circuit (1=primary, 2=secondary, 3=tertiary). Drives automated routing logic and operational decision-making during TSF transitions.

attributes.name: routing_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of this routing configuration. ACTIVE routings are currently in use, PLANNED are future configurations, INACTIVE are temporarily suspended, DECOMMISSIONED are permanently retired.

attributes.name: tailings_destination_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the Tailings Storage Facility (TSF) or waste stream destination for tailings generated by this circuit. Critical for environmental compliance, TSF capacity planning, and regulatory reporting. [Moved from processing_circuit: This attribute in processing_circuit currently stores a single TSF destination code, implying a 1:N relationship. In the true M:N business reality where circuits can route to multiple TSFs based on operational conditions, this attribute should be removed and replaced by the circuit_tailings_routing association which captures the full many-to-many routing configuration with time-based and priority-based routing rules.]
attributes.references: ISO 14001; ICMM Tailings Management; GRI 306; IsoMetrix

attributes.name: tailings_stream_designation
attributes.description: Classification of the tailings stream type for this routing (e.g., PRIMARY for main tailings flow, ARD for acid-generating tailings requiring lined storage, BENIGN for non-reactive tailings, EMERGENCY for overflow routing). Drives environmental compliance and TSF selection logic.

products.name: circuit_product_configuration
products.description: This association product represents the operational configuration between a processing circuit and a saleable product it can produce. It captures the target metallurgical performance parameters, production priority, and configuration settings specific to each circuit-product combination. Each record links one processing circuit to one saleable product with attributes that exist only in the context of this production relationship. This enables flexible processing operations where circuits can be configured to produce different products through different operating modes (cleaner/scavenger splits, grade campaigns) and where products can be sourced from multiple circuits (primary/secondary lines, parallel processing trains).. Existence Justification: In flexible mineral processing operations, a single processing circuit can be configured to produce multiple saleable products through different operating modes (cleaner vs. scavenger splits, grade campaigns, bulk vs. premium production). Conversely, a single saleable product can be produced by multiple circuits (primary and secondary processing lines, parallel circuit trains, backup circuits). The business actively manages these circuit-product configurations with specific metallurgical targets, production priorities, and operating parameters for each combination.

attributes.name: circuit_product_configuration_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each circuit-product configuration record. Primary key for the association.

attributes.name: circuit_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Circuit Product Configuration - Processing Circuit Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the processing circuit that is configured to produce the saleable product

attributes.name: saleable_product_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Circuit Product Configuration - Saleable Product Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the saleable product that can be produced by the processing circuit

attributes.name: circuit_configuration_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the specific operating configuration or mode used when producing this product from this circuit (e.g., CLEANER_ONLY, SCAV_RECYCLE, HIGH_GRADE_CAMPAIGN, BULK_PRODUCTION). Captures the operational setup that differentiates how different products are produced.

attributes.name: concentrate_product_code
attributes.description: Product code of the primary output concentrate or processed product from this circuit (e.g., CU-CON-01 for copper concentrate). Links to sales contracts, logistics, and product quality specifications. [Moved from processing_circuit: This attribute in processing_circuit currently captures a single primary output product code. In a flexible processing operation where circuits can produce multiple products, this attribute should be removed from the circuit entity and the relationship should be captured through the circuit_product_configuration association. Each circuit-product configuration record will link to the saleable_product via FK, eliminating the need for a single product code on the circuit.]
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA SD; JORC Code; CIM Standards

attributes.name: configuration_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this circuit-product configuration. ACTIVE: currently in production use; PLANNED: approved for future implementation; SUSPENDED: temporarily inactive; DECOMMISSIONED: permanently retired; TESTING: under commissioning or trial.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this circuit-product configuration record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this circuit-product configuration ceased or will cease to be active. Null indicates currently active configuration. Enables tracking of configuration lifecycle.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to any field in this circuit-product configuration record.

attributes.name: production_priority
attributes.description: Integer ranking indicating the priority of this product within the circuit's production portfolio. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used for production scheduling and campaign planning when a circuit can produce multiple products.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this circuit-product configuration became or becomes active and operational. Enables tracking of configuration history and future planned configurations.

attributes.name: target_grade_pct
attributes.description: Target product grade for this specific circuit-product combination expressed as a percentage of valuable mineral content. This is configuration-specific as different products from the same circuit may have different grade targets (e.g., cleaner concentrate vs. rougher concentrate).

attributes.name: target_recovery_pct
attributes.description: Target metallurgical recovery rate for this specific circuit-product combination expressed as a percentage. This is configuration-specific and may differ from the circuit's general design recovery rate depending on the product being produced and operating mode.

products.name: tailings_routing
products.description: This association product represents the operational routing configuration between processing plants and Tailings Storage Facilities. It captures the physical pipeline connections, slurry specifications, and operational parameters that govern how tailings from each processing plant are delivered to each TSF. Each record links one processing plant to one TSF with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific routing relationship, including commissioning dates, slurry density specifications, stream type classification, and primary destination designation.. Existence Justification: In large mining operations, processing plants routinely route tailings to multiple TSFs based on operational requirements, capacity constraints, and contingency planning. For example, Olympic Dam operates multiple processing circuits (oxide, sulphide) that can route to different TSF cells or compartments. Conversely, a single TSF may receive tailings from multiple processing plants on the same mine site. The business actively manages these routing configurations, tracking pipeline infrastructure, slurry specifications, commissioning dates, and primary vs. emergency destination designations for each plant-TSF connection.

attributes.name: tailings_routing_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for this specific plant-to-TSF routing configuration. Primary key for the tailings routing association.

attributes.name: pipeline_id
attributes.description: Business identifier for the physical tailings pipeline that connects this processing plant to this TSF. Multiple plants may share pipeline infrastructure or a single plant may have dedicated pipelines to different TSFs. This attribute belongs to the routing relationship because it represents the physical connection infrastructure specific to this plant-TSF pair.

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the source processing plant that generates the tailings stream

attributes.name: tsf_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the destination Tailings Storage Facility that receives the tailings stream

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when this specific plant-to-TSF routing configuration was commissioned and became operational. This is distinct from the plant commissioning date or TSF commissioning date because routing connections are established independently as infrastructure is built or modified. Critical for tracking operational history and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: decommissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when this specific plant-to-TSF routing configuration was decommissioned and ceased operation. Null if the routing is still active. Routing may be decommissioned when TSFs reach capacity, pipelines are retired, or plant operations are reconfigured, even if both the plant and TSF remain operational with other routing configurations.

attributes.name: design_flow_rate_m3ph
attributes.description: Design volumetric flow rate of tailings slurry through this routing configuration, expressed in cubic meters per hour (m³/h). This is specific to the routing because it depends on pipeline diameter, pump capacity, elevation change, and distance between the specific plant and TSF. Critical for hydraulic design and operational planning.

attributes.name: design_slurry_density_pct
attributes.description: Design solids content of the tailings slurry for this specific plant-to-TSF routing, expressed as percentage by weight (0-100). This varies by routing because different TSFs may require different slurry densities based on dam design, deposition method, and storage capacity constraints. Critical for pipeline design, pumping requirements, and TSF water balance.

attributes.name: elevation_gain_m
attributes.description: Net elevation gain (or loss if negative) from the processing plant discharge point to the TSF deposition point for this specific routing, measured in meters. This is a relationship attribute because it describes the topographic profile of this specific plant-TSF connection. Critical for pump sizing and energy consumption calculations.

attributes.name: is_primary_destination
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this TSF is the primary (normal operating) destination for tailings from this processing plant. True = primary destination; False = secondary/emergency destination. A plant typically has one primary TSF and may have one or more secondary TSFs for contingency operations, maintenance periods, or capacity management. This attribute belongs to the routing relationship because it describes the operational priority of this specific plant-TSF connection.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of this specific plant-to-TSF routing configuration. Active = currently in use; Standby = commissioned but not currently routing tailings (emergency backup); Decommissioned = permanently retired; Under-construction = pipeline and infrastructure being built. This status is independent of the plant and TSF operational statuses because routing configurations can be in standby while both endpoints are active.

attributes.name: pipeline_length_km
attributes.description: Total length of the tailings pipeline for this specific plant-to-TSF routing, measured in kilometers. This is a relationship attribute because it describes the physical connection infrastructure between this specific plant-TSF pair. Relevant for pumping energy calculations, maintenance planning, and risk assessment.

attributes.name: tailings_stream_type
attributes.description: Classification of the tailings stream type being routed from this plant to this TSF. Conventional tailings are slurry with 20-30% solids; thickened tailings are 45-55% solids; paste tailings are 65-75% solids; filtered tailings are dewatered to 80%+ solids; co-disposal includes waste rock. This attribute belongs to the routing relationship because the same plant may produce different stream types for different TSFs depending on processing method and TSF design requirements.

products.name: plant_product_campaign
products.description: This association product represents the production campaign relationship between processing_plant and saleable_product. It captures the operational reality that a single processing plant runs multiple production campaigns over time, each targeting a specific saleable product variant, and that a single saleable product can be produced by multiple plants across the mining operation. Each record represents one production campaign linking one processing plant to one saleable product with campaign-specific attributes including scheduling, target rates, actual production volumes, and quality outcomes achieved.. Existence Justification: In mining operations, processing plants run production campaigns where they switch between producing different saleable product variants based on ore feed characteristics, market demand, and operational optimization. A single plant produces multiple products over time (e.g., different concentrate grades, lump vs fines splits), and a single saleable product is produced by multiple plants across the mining operation. Production campaigns are actively managed operational entities with specific start/end dates, target rates, actual production volumes, and quality outcomes.

attributes.name: plant_product_campaign_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Plant Product Campaign - Plant Product Campaign Id
attributes.description: Primary key for the plant_product_campaign association

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Plant Product Campaign - Processing Plant Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the processing plant facility executing this production campaign

attributes.name: saleable_product_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Plant Product Campaign - Saleable Product Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the saleable product variant being produced in this campaign

attributes.name: actual_production_tonnes
attributes.description: Cumulative actual production volume achieved during this campaign expressed in dry metric tonnes. Updated as production progresses. Used for campaign performance analysis and variance reporting.

attributes.name: campaign_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for this production campaign used in operational reporting and plant scheduling systems

attributes.name: campaign_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this production campaign concluded or is planned to conclude. Null for ongoing campaigns. Used for campaign duration analysis and scheduling.

attributes.name: campaign_notes
attributes.description: Free-text operational notes capturing campaign-specific conditions, challenges, process adjustments, or quality issues encountered during production.

attributes.name: campaign_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which this production campaign commenced. Represents when the plant began processing ore to produce this specific saleable product variant.

attributes.name: campaign_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the production campaign. Planned: scheduled but not started; Active: currently producing; Suspended: temporarily halted; Completed: finished successfully; Cancelled: terminated before completion.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this production campaign record was first created in the system

attributes.name: feed_ore_source
attributes.description: Identification of the primary ore source (pit, stockpile, or blend) feeding this production campaign. Critical for traceability and understanding quality variations.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to any field in this production campaign record

attributes.name: quality_grade_achieved_pct
attributes.description: Average grade of the valuable mineral component achieved in the saleable product during this campaign, expressed as percentage. Campaign-specific quality outcome that may vary from target grade specification based on feed ore characteristics and plant performance.

attributes.name: recovery_rate_achieved_pct
attributes.description: Actual metallurgical recovery rate achieved during this campaign expressed as percentage. Campaign-specific performance metric comparing valuable mineral in product to valuable mineral in feed.

attributes.name: target_production_rate_tph
attributes.description: Planned throughput rate for this campaign expressed in dry metric tonnes per hour (tph). Campaign-specific target that may differ from plant nameplate capacity based on ore characteristics and product specifications.

products.name: plant_community_contribution
products.description: This association product represents the financial and operational contribution relationship between processing plants and community investment programs. It captures the multi-site funding model where individual processing plants contribute to shared community programs, and programs receive funding from multiple plant facilities. Each record links one processing plant to one community investment program with contribution amounts, participation levels, funding periods, and reporting obligations that exist only in the context of this specific plant-program relationship.. Existence Justification: In mining operations, community investment programs are frequently funded by multiple processing plants as part of multi-site CSR strategies, particularly when programs serve regions with multiple facilities. Conversely, individual processing plants contribute to multiple community programs across different focus areas (education, health, infrastructure) to fulfill their social licence obligations. The business actively manages these contribution relationships, tracking contribution amounts, participation levels, funding periods, and reporting obligations specific to each plant-program pair.

attributes.name: plant_community_contribution_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for this plant-program contribution record. Primary key.

attributes.name: investment_program_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Plant Community Contribution - Community Investment Program Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the community investment program receiving the contribution from the processing plant

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Plant Community Contribution - Processing Plant Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the processing plant facility making the contribution to the community investment program

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when this specific plant's contribution to this program was formally approved by the plant's management or the corporate CSR committee.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the executive, plant manager, or committee that approved this plant's contribution to the community investment program.

attributes.name: benefit_sharing_agreement_clause
attributes.description: Reference to the specific clause or section in the benefit-sharing agreement that governs this plant's contribution obligations to this program.

attributes.name: contribution_amount
attributes.description: The monetary contribution amount from this specific processing plant to this specific community investment program. Represents the plant's share of program funding.

attributes.name: contribution_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the contribution amount (e.g., USD, AUD, CAD, ZAR). May differ from the program's budget currency if plants operate in different jurisdictions.

attributes.name: contribution_status
attributes.description: Current status of this plant's contribution to the program: committed (pledged but not yet active), active (currently funding), suspended (temporarily paused), completed (funding period ended), or cancelled (commitment withdrawn).

attributes.name: contribution_type
attributes.description: The nature of the contribution from the processing plant to the program: direct_funding (cash), in_kind (goods/services), technical_support, infrastructure, equipment, or personnel secondment.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this plant-program contribution record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: funding_period_end
attributes.description: The date when this processing plant's contribution commitment to this community investment program ends. May differ from the program's overall end date if plants have different commitment periods.

attributes.name: funding_period_start
attributes.description: The date when this processing plant's contribution commitment to this community investment program begins. May differ from the program's overall start date if plants join at different times.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this plant-program contribution record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: program_participation_level
attributes.description: The level of involvement and responsibility this processing plant has in the community investment program: primary_sponsor (lead funder), co_sponsor (major partner), supporting (moderate contribution), or minor_contributor.

attributes.name: reporting_obligation
attributes.description: Description of the specific reporting requirements and obligations this processing plant has for this community investment program, including frequency, format, and content of progress reports tied to this plant's contribution.

products.name: stockpile_tenement_contribution
products.description: This association product represents the contribution relationship between concentrate stockpiles and source tenements in mining operations. It captures the blended origin of concentrate inventory, tracking which tenements contributed material to which stockpiles, with tonnage, grade, and time period attribution. Each record links one concentrate stockpile to one source tenement with contribution metrics required for royalty allocation, origin certification, and mine-to-market traceability.. Existence Justification: In mining operations, concentrate stockpiles are blended inventories containing material from multiple source tenements, and each tenement's production contributes to multiple stockpile batches over time as mining progresses. The business actively manages these contribution relationships to allocate royalties to the correct tenement holders, certify product origin for customers, and reconcile blend composition against production plans. This is an operational tracking requirement, not an analytical correlation.

attributes.name: stockpile_tenement_contribution_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each stockpile-tenement contribution record

attributes.name: concentrate_stockpile_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Stockpile Tenement Contribution - Concentrate Stockpile Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the concentrate stockpile that received material from the source tenement

attributes.name: tenement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the source tenement that contributed material to the stockpile

attributes.name: average_grade_pct
attributes.description: Average assay grade (%) of the concentrate contributed from this tenement during the source production period. Used for blend quality reconciliation and tenement performance tracking.

attributes.name: contribution_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of the stockpile's total inventory contributed by this tenement, calculated as (contribution_tonnage_dmt / stockpile.inventory_dmt) * 100. Used for blend composition reporting.

attributes.name: contribution_status
attributes.description: Lifecycle status of this contribution record. active: material still in stockpile; depleted: material shipped out; reconciled: final tonnage confirmed; disputed: under investigation for grade or tonnage variance.

attributes.name: contribution_tonnage_dmt
attributes.description: Dry metric tonnes of concentrate contributed from this tenement to this stockpile during the source production period. Used for royalty allocation and origin certification.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this contribution record, reflecting changes to tonnage, grade, or status during reconciliation processes.

attributes.name: recorded_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this contribution record was created in the system, typically when material from the tenement was added to the stockpile.

attributes.name: royalty_allocation_amount
attributes.description: Calculated royalty amount (in local currency) attributable to this tenement's contribution to the stockpile, based on contribution tonnage and the tenement's royalty rate. Used for financial accrual and payment processing.

attributes.name: source_production_period_end
attributes.description: End date of the production period during which this tenement's material was added to the stockpile. Supports traceability and time-based royalty calculations.

attributes.name: source_production_period_start
attributes.description: Start date of the production period during which this tenement's material was added to the stockpile. Supports traceability and time-based royalty calculations.

products.name: circuit_delivery
products.description: This association product represents the delivery event between a capital project and a processing circuit. It captures the commissioning, handover, and performance acceptance of a processing circuit as delivered by a capital project. Each record links one capital project to one processing circuit with attributes that exist only in the context of this project delivery relationship, including commissioning dates, performance test outcomes, handover status, and defects liability tracking.. Existence Justification: In mining capital projects, large brownfield expansion projects routinely deliver multiple processing circuits simultaneously (e.g., one project delivers primary crushing, secondary grinding, and flotation circuits). Conversely, individual processing circuits undergo upgrades, modifications, and capacity expansions through multiple capital projects over their operational life. The business actively manages circuit delivery as a formal handover process with commissioning milestones, performance testing, acceptance criteria, and defects liability tracking.

attributes.name: circuit_delivery_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for this circuit delivery record, serving as the primary key for the association between a capital project and a processing circuit

attributes.name: capital_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the capital project responsible for delivering this processing circuit

attributes.name: circuit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the processing circuit being delivered by this capital project

attributes.name: actual_delivery_cost
attributes.description: Actual capital expenditure incurred to deliver this specific processing circuit as part of the broader capital project. Used for cost tracking and variance analysis at circuit level.

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date on which this specific processing circuit was commissioned as part of this capital project. Marks the formal acceptance of the circuit into operational testing phase.

attributes.name: defects_liability_period_months
attributes.description: Duration in months of the defects liability period during which the project team or contractor remains responsible for rectifying defects in the delivered circuit. Typically 12-24 months from provisional acceptance.

attributes.name: delivery_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing key observations, issues, lessons learned, or special conditions related to the delivery of this circuit by this project

attributes.name: design_capacity_achieved_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the delivered processing circuit achieved its nameplate design capacity during performance testing. Used to track project delivery success and trigger milestone payments.

attributes.name: final_acceptance_date
attributes.description: Date on which the processing circuit received final acceptance after successful completion of the defects liability period, formally closing out the project delivery obligation

attributes.name: handover_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the circuit handover process from the project team to operations. Tracks progression through construction, commissioning, testing, acceptance, and defects liability phases.

attributes.name: performance_test_date
attributes.description: Date on which performance acceptance testing was conducted for this circuit delivery to verify that design throughput, recovery rates, and other KPIs meet contractual specifications

attributes.name: provisional_acceptance_date
attributes.description: Date on which the processing circuit was provisionally accepted by operations, marking the start of the defects liability period and transfer of operational responsibility

products.name: plant_contractor_engagement
products.description: This association product represents the engagement contract between a processing plant and a contractor. It captures the specific work assignment, duration, access permissions, and work scope for each contractor engaged at each processing plant. Each record links one processing plant to one contractor with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific engagement relationship.. Existence Justification: In mining operations, contractors are engaged across multiple processing plants for specialized work (maintenance campaigns, shutdowns, commissioning projects), and each processing plant simultaneously engages multiple contractors across different trades (mechanical, electrical, civil, instrumentation). The engagement relationship is actively managed with plant-specific work scopes, access zones, permits, and billing rates that vary by plant and contractor combination.

attributes.name: plant_contractor_engagement_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for this specific engagement relationship between a processing plant and a contractor. Primary key.

attributes.name: contractor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the contractor engaged at the processing plant

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Plant Contractor Engagement - Processing Plant Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the processing plant where the contractor is engaged

attributes.name: supervisor_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the plant employee (supervisor or superintendent) responsible for overseeing this contractor's work at this plant. Used for accountability and escalation.

attributes.name: daily_rate_aud
attributes.description: Daily billing rate in Australian dollars for this contractor at this specific plant. May vary by plant due to remoteness, FIFO arrangements, or specialized equipment requirements.

attributes.name: engagement_end_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual end date of this contractor engagement at this processing plant. Null for ongoing engagements. Used for workforce planning and access expiry.

attributes.name: engagement_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which this specific contractor engagement at this processing plant commenced. Used for tenure calculation and access control validation.

attributes.name: engagement_status
attributes.description: Current status of this plant-contractor engagement. Active = contractor currently working; Suspended = temporarily paused; Completed = engagement finished as planned; Terminated = engagement ended early.

attributes.name: permit_to_work_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the permit-to-work authorization for this contractor engagement at this plant. Links to HSE permit management system for high-risk work activities.

attributes.name: roster_pattern
attributes.description: Work roster pattern for this contractor at this plant (e.g., '2-weeks-on-1-week-off', '8-days-on-6-days-off', 'day-shift-only'). Plant-specific roster arrangements.

attributes.name: site_access_zones
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of plant zones and areas this contractor is authorized to access for this engagement (e.g., 'crushing-circuit,flotation-area,control-room,maintenance-workshop'). Plant-specific access control.

attributes.name: work_scope
attributes.description: Detailed description of the work scope and responsibilities for this contractor at this specific processing plant (e.g., 'SAG mill maintenance', 'flotation circuit electrical work', 'shutdown campaign - conveyor systems').

products.name: measurement_point
products.description: Master reference table for measurement_point. Referenced by measurement_point_id.

attributes.name: measurement_point_id
attributes.description: Primary key for measurement_point

attributes.name: asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific equipment or asset where the measurement instrument is installed (e.g., SAG mill, flotation cell, thickener).

attributes.name: process_area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the process area or circuit section where this measurement point is located (e.g., comminution, flotation, dewatering).

domains.name: laboratory
domains.description: Manages sample lifecycle, assay workflows, QA/QC protocols, and analytical results via LIMS (LabWare). Serves as the SSOT for all geochemical and metallurgical test data including fire assay, XRF, and leach test results that underpin resource estimation and process optimisation.

products.name: laboratory_sample
products.description: Master record for every physical sample submitted to the laboratory, covering drill core (HQ, NQ, PQ), RC chips, channel samples, process stream samples, and metallurgical test charges. Captures sample identity, origin (drill hole ID, bench, pit, process stream), sample type, weight, preparation method, chain-of-custody status, LIMS barcode, and spatial coordinates (from/to depth or location). This is the SSOT for all sample identity data in LabWare LIMS and underpins resource estimation, grade control, and process optimisation workflows.

attributes.description: Starting depth in meters for the sample interval within the drill hole or channel. Used for spatial correlation with geological models and resource estimation.

attributes.description: Easting coordinate (X) of the sample collection point in the mine coordinate system. Used for spatial analysis and integration with geological models.

attributes.description: Elevation (Z) of the sample collection point in meters above sea level. Completes the 3D spatial coordinates for geological modeling.

attributes.description: Northing coordinate (Y) of the sample collection point in the mine coordinate system. Used for spatial analysis and integration with geological models.

attributes.description: Date and time when this sample record was last modified in the LIMS system. Part of audit trail for data governance.

attributes.description: Name of the open pit or mining area from which the sample was collected. Applicable for grade control and production samples.

attributes.description: Sample preparation technique applied before analysis. Crush and split for coarse reduction; pulverize for fine grinding; dry for moisture removal; wet screen for size separation; no prep for direct analysis.
attributes.references: ISO 3081 Sample Preparation for Iron Ores

attributes.name: process_stream_name
attributes.description: Name of the processing plant stream from which the sample was collected (e.g., ROM feed, crusher discharge, flotation concentrate, tailings). Applicable for process stream samples.

attributes.name: pulp_weight_g
attributes.description: Weight in grams of the pulverized sample (pulp) prepared for assay analysis. Typically 200-500g depending on analytical method and commodity.

attributes.name: qaqc_type
attributes.description: Classification of the sample for quality control purposes. Field duplicate tests sampling precision; lab duplicate tests analytical precision; standard tests accuracy; blank tests contamination; unknown is a regular production sample.
attributes.references: JORC Code Quality Assurance and Quality Control (QA/QC) Guidelines

attributes.name: received_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the sample was received and registered in the laboratory LIMS. Used to track turnaround time and chain-of-custody.

attributes.name: retention_period_days
attributes.description: Number of days the sample or its pulp must be retained before disposal, as per regulatory or company policy. Typically 90-365 days depending on sample type and jurisdiction.

attributes.name: sample_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the sample, typically a barcode or sequential number assigned by LIMS at sample registration. Used for chain-of-custody tracking and laboratory workflows.

attributes.name: sample_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the sample in the laboratory workflow. Tracks progression from registration through preparation, analysis, completion, and archival or rejection. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: registered|prepared|submitted|in_analysis|completed|archived|rejected — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: sample_type
attributes.description: Classification of the sample based on its origin and purpose. Drill core samples (HQ, NQ, PQ) are from diamond drilling; RC (Reverse Circulation) chips are from percussion drilling; channel samples are from underground faces; process stream samples are from plant operations; metallurgical test charges are for beneficiation studies; quality control samples are standards and blanks.

attributes.name: storage_location
attributes.description: Physical location where the sample or its pulp/reject is stored after analysis. Used for sample retrieval and archival management.

attributes.name: submitted_by

attributes.name: accuracy_percent
attributes.description: Calculated accuracy of the assay result compared to the expected grade for standard reference materials, expressed as a percentage. Measures systematic bias in the analytical method.

attributes.name: analysis_date
attributes.description: The date on which the assay analysis was performed. Critical for tracking sample turnaround time and ensuring results are used within appropriate timeframes for resource estimation and grade control.

attributes.name: analysis_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the assay analysis was completed. Provides granular traceability for quality control and audit purposes.

attributes.name: analyte_code
attributes.description: Standard code representing the element or compound analyzed (e.g., AU for gold, CU for copper, FE for iron, S for sulfur). Follows periodic table symbols or industry-standard compound codes.

attributes.name: analyte_name
attributes.description: Full name of the element or compound analyzed (e.g., Gold, Copper, Iron, Sulfur, Arsenic). Human-readable description of the analyte.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this assay result was formally approved by a qualified person. Marks the transition from preliminary to certified status.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Identifier of the qualified person or laboratory supervisor who reviewed and approved this assay result for release. Required for certified results used in resource estimation.

attributes.name: below_detection_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the assay result was below the detection limit of the analytical method. True if below detection, False otherwise. Results flagged as below detection are typically assigned half the detection limit value for statistical purposes.

attributes.name: certified_result_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this assay result has been certified and approved for use in JORC/NI 43-101 resource estimation and public reporting. True if certified, False if preliminary or for internal use only.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for analyst or reviewer comments regarding the assay result, including notes on sample condition, analytical issues, QA/QC observations, or special handling requirements.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this assay result record was first created in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS). Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: detection_limit
attributes.description: The minimum concentration of the analyte that can be reliably detected by the analytical method. Results below this threshold are typically reported as below detection limit (BDL) or less than (<) values.

attributes.name: dilution_factor
attributes.description: The factor by which the sample was diluted prior to analysis, typically applied when initial results exceed the upper detection limit. A value of 1.0 indicates no dilution; values greater than 1.0 indicate the sample was diluted (e.g., 10.0 means 10x dilution).

attributes.name: expected_grade
attributes.description: The certified or expected grade value for a standard reference material. Used to calculate accuracy and bias in QA/QC analysis. Null for non-standard samples.

attributes.name: grade_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the reported grade. Common units include ppm (parts per million), percent (%), g/t (grams per tonne), oz/t (ounces per ton), mg/kg (milligrams per kilogram), ppb (parts per billion).

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this assay result record was last modified in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS). Tracks changes for audit and quality control purposes.

attributes.name: over_limit_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the initial assay result exceeded the upper detection limit of the analytical method, requiring dilution and re-analysis. True if over limit, False otherwise.

attributes.name: precision_percent
attributes.description: Calculated precision of the assay result based on duplicate sample analysis, expressed as a percentage. Measures random error and reproducibility of the analytical method.

attributes.name: qaqc_sample_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QA/QC) Sample Type
attributes.description: Identifies the type of QA/QC sample if this result is part of the quality control program. Original indicates a regular production sample; other values indicate QA/QC control samples inserted into the analytical stream.

attributes.name: qaqc_status
attributes.description: Status of quality assurance and quality control checks applied to this assay result. Indicates whether the result passed all QA/QC protocols including blank, duplicate, and standard reference material checks.

attributes.name: reported_date
attributes.description: The date on which the assay result was officially reported and released from the laboratory to the requesting party. May differ from analysis date due to quality control review and approval workflows.

attributes.name: reported_grade
attributes.description: The final assay grade value reported for the analyte in the sample. This is the primary geochemical measurement used for resource estimation, grade control, and metallurgical balance calculations. May be expressed in various units depending on analyte (ppm, percent, g/t).

attributes.name: result_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the assay result. Preliminary results are for internal use only; final results are certified for resource estimation; cancelled results have been invalidated; superseded results have been replaced by re-analysis.

attributes.name: upper_limit
attributes.description: The maximum concentration of the analyte that can be accurately measured by the analytical method without dilution. Results exceeding this threshold require sample dilution and re-analysis.

products.name: metallurgical_test
products.description: Records all metallurgical test programs conducted on ore samples including comminution tests (Bond Work Index BWi/RWi, SAG Mill Comminution SMC, JK Drop Weight, HPGR, Abrasion Index), flotation tests (batch, locked cycle for Cu, Ni, Pb-Zn, Li spodumene), leach tests (bottle roll, column, heap, agitation, CIL/CIP for Au, Cu, Li), DMS, and SX-EW tests. Captures test type, feed grade, product grade, recovery rate, reagent consumption, grind size (P80), test conditions (pH, Eh, temperature, duration), and time-series extraction data. Serves as SSOT for all metallurgical characterisation data underpinning process design, feasibility studies, and plant optimisation.
