attributes.description: Indicates whether the rehabilitation expenditure is classified as Operating Expenditure (OPEX) or Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) for internal cost reporting and All-In Sustaining Cost (AISC) calculation purposes.
attributes.references: AISC Reporting Standard (World Gold Council); SAP S/4HANA CO Module; IFRS Financial Statements

attributes.name: provision_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing material assumptions, significant judgements, regulatory conditions, or other contextual information relevant to the rehabilitation provision estimate and its movements during the period.
attributes.references: IAS 37 Paragraph 85; IFRS Financial Statements Disclosure Requirements

attributes.name: provision_reference
attributes.description: Externally-known business reference code for the provision record, used in SAP FI/CO and regulatory financial disclosures. Follows the format REHAB-<SITE_CODE>-<YEAR>.
attributes.references: IAS 37; IFRS 6 Exploration for and Evaluation of Mineral Resources; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

attributes.name: provision_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the rehabilitation provision record. Active indicates the provision is live on the balance sheet; revised indicates a formal estimate revision has been processed; settled indicates actual expenditure has fully drawn down the provision; closed indicates the mine site rehabilitation obligation has been discharged; under_review indicates the provision is being reassessed.
attributes.references: IAS 37 Paragraphs 14–26; ICMM Mine Closure Framework

attributes.name: provision_type
attributes.description: Classification of the nature of the rehabilitation obligation. Decommissioning covers plant and equipment removal; rehabilitation covers land and soil restoration; environmental_restoration covers broader ecosystem recovery; tailings_remediation covers Tailings Storage Facility (TSF) closure; water_treatment covers ongoing water management post-closure; infrastructure_removal covers roads, buildings, and utilities. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: decommissioning|rehabilitation|environmental_restoration|tailings_remediation|water_treatment|infrastructure_removal — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAS 37; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems; ICMM Mine Closure Framework

attributes.name: recognition_date
attributes.description: The date on which the rehabilitation provision was first recognised on the balance sheet, corresponding to the date the constructive or legal obligation arose (typically commencement of mining disturbance).

attributes.name: regulatory_bond_amount
attributes.description: The financial assurance bond amount lodged with the relevant government regulator as security for the rehabilitation obligation. May differ from the IAS 37 provision balance due to different regulatory vs. accounting methodologies.
attributes.references: ICMM Mine Closure Framework; ISO 14001; State/Territory Mining Acts; Environmental Impact Statement (EIS)

attributes.name: rehabilitation_completed_area_ha
attributes.description: The cumulative area of land (in hectares) that has been successfully rehabilitated and formally signed off by the relevant environmental regulator, reducing the outstanding rehabilitation obligation.
attributes.references: ISO 14001; ICMM Mine Closure Framework; Environmental Impact Statement (EIS)

attributes.name: reporting_period_end_date
attributes.description: The financial reporting period end date (balance sheet date) to which this provision balance snapshot relates. Enables period-over-period tracking of provision movements.
attributes.references: IAS 37; IFRS Financial Statements; SAP S/4HANA FI Closing Operations

attributes.name: revision_amount
attributes.description: Net increase or decrease to the provision balance arising from revisions to the estimated future rehabilitation cost during the period. Positive values indicate upward revisions; negative values indicate downward revisions. Corresponds to changes in the underlying asset under IFRIC 1.
attributes.references: IAS 37; IFRIC 1 Changes in Existing Decommissioning, Restoration and Similar Liabilities

attributes.name: sap_provision_document_number
attributes.description: The SAP FI accounting document number under which the rehabilitation provision journal entry is posted in the general ledger. Enables traceability between the data product and the source system of record.

attributes.name: tsf_related_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rehabilitation provision relates specifically to a Tailings Storage Facility (TSF) closure obligation, which carries heightened regulatory scrutiny and disclosure requirements under ICMM and MAC standards.
attributes.references: ICMM Mine Closure Framework; Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management (GISTM); ISO 14001

attributes.name: undiscounted_cost_estimate
attributes.description: The total estimated future cost of mine rehabilitation and closure in nominal (undiscounted) terms, as determined by the most recent mine closure cost estimate study. This is the gross cost before applying the time-value-of-money discount.
attributes.references: IAS 37; ICMM Mine Closure Framework; JORC Code

attributes.name: unwinding_of_discount_amount
attributes.description: The finance charge recognised in the income statement during the period representing the unwinding of the time-value-of-money discount applied to the provision. Calculated as the opening provision balance multiplied by the pre-tax risk-free discount rate.
attributes.references: IAS 37 Paragraph 60; IFRIC 1; IFRS Financial Statements

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this rehabilitation provision record was most recently modified, supporting audit trail requirements and change tracking for IAS 37 provision movement disclosures.
attributes.references: IAS 37; SAP S/4HANA FI Audit Trail; IFRS Financial Statements

attributes.name: years_to_closure
attributes.description: The number of years from the reporting period end date to the expected mine closure date, used as the discounting period in the present value calculation of the rehabilitation provision.

products.name: fixed_asset
products.description: Fixed asset master from SAP FI Asset Accounting capturing all capitalised mining assets including plant and equipment, mine development costs, mineral rights, and infrastructure. Tracks acquisition cost, accumulated depreciation, net book value, useful life, depreciation method (units of production or straight-line), and asset class. Supports CAPEX reporting and balance sheet disclosures.

attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the fixed asset record in the data lakehouse. Primary key for the fixed_asset data product.

attributes.name: accumulated_depreciation
attributes.description: Total depreciation charged against the asset from the acquisition date to the current reporting period. Corresponds to SAP ANLC-KNAFA. Used to calculate net book value for balance sheet reporting.

attributes.name: acquisition_cost
attributes.description: Original historical cost of the asset at the time of acquisition or capitalisation, including purchase price, installation, and directly attributable costs. Corresponds to SAP ANLC-KANSW. Reported in the asset's book currency.

attributes.name: acquisition_date
attributes.description: Date on which the fixed asset was acquired, capitalised, or placed in service. Used as the start date for depreciation calculations and CAPEX reporting. Corresponds to SAP ANLA-AKTIV.

attributes.name: asset_category
attributes.description: High-level business category of the fixed asset used for CAPEX reporting and balance sheet disclosures. Aligns with IAS 16 and IFRS 6 asset groupings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: plant_and_equipment|mine_development|mineral_rights|infrastructure|mobile_equipment|land|construction_in_progress — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAS 16; IFRS 6; IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards)

attributes.name: asset_class_code
attributes.description: SAP FI-AA asset class code (ANLA-ANLKL) that classifies the asset into categories such as plant and equipment, mine development costs, mineral rights, infrastructure, or vehicles. Drives depreciation rules and balance sheet grouping.

attributes.name: asset_description
attributes.description: Short descriptive name of the fixed asset as recorded in SAP FI-AA (ANLA-TXT50). Examples: 'SAG Mill No. 3', 'Haul Road – Pit 2 to ROM Pad', 'Mineral Rights – Tenement ML1234'.

attributes.name: asset_number
attributes.description: The externally-known SAP FI-AA asset number uniquely identifying the capitalised asset within the asset accounting module. Corresponds to the SAP ANLA-ANLN1 field.

attributes.name: asset_responsible_person
attributes.description: Name or personnel number of the individual accountable for the asset's physical custody, condition, and compliance with asset management policies. Corresponds to SAP ANLA-VERTN.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; ISO 55001 Asset Management

attributes.name: asset_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the fixed asset. 'active' indicates the asset is in service and depreciating; 'under_construction' indicates a capital work in progress (CWIP); 'retired' indicates end of useful life; 'disposed' indicates sale or write-off; 'impaired' indicates a recognised impairment loss; 'transferred' indicates inter-company or inter-site transfer.

attributes.name: asset_sub_number
attributes.description: SAP FI-AA sub-number (ANLN2) used to track components or partial retirements of a main asset number. Enables component-level tracking within a single asset master.

attributes.name: asset_tag_number
attributes.description: Physical asset tag or barcode number affixed to the asset for field identification and inventory verification. Used during physical asset counts and reconciliation with the SAP asset register.

attributes.name: business_area_code
attributes.description: SAP FI business area code associated with the asset, used for segment reporting and internal financial statements across mining operations.

attributes.name: capex_budget_code
attributes.description: Reference code linking the asset to the approved CAPEX budget line item or capital project authorisation. Supports CAPEX tracking and variance reporting against approved capital expenditure budgets.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA PS/CO; CAPEX reporting; IFRS

attributes.name: capitalisation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the asset was formally capitalised and transferred from capital work in progress (CWIP) to a fixed asset class. May differ from acquisition_date for assets under construction.

attributes.name: company_code
attributes.description: SAP FI company code (BUKRS) to which the fixed asset belongs. Identifies the legal entity responsible for the asset for financial reporting and balance sheet purposes.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the fixed asset master record was first created in the source system (SAP FI-AA). Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; IFRS audit requirements

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the asset's financial values (acquisition cost, depreciation, NBV) are recorded. Typically the company code currency (e.g., AUD, USD, ZAR).

attributes.name: deactivation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the asset was retired, disposed of, or decommissioned. Marks the end of the asset's depreciable life in the accounting records.

attributes.name: depreciation_key
attributes.description: SAP FI-AA depreciation key code (e.g., LINR, DG10, UOP1) that defines the specific depreciation calculation rules applied to the asset, including method, period control, and base value.

attributes.name: depreciation_method
attributes.description: Accounting method used to calculate periodic depreciation for the asset. Mining assets commonly use 'units_of_production' (UOP) aligned to ore reserve depletion or 'straight_line' over useful life. Corresponds to SAP depreciation key configuration.

attributes.name: ifrs6_exploration_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the asset is classified as an exploration and evaluation asset under IFRS 6 (Exploration for and Evaluation of Mineral Resources). When true, specific IFRS 6 recognition and impairment rules apply rather than standard IAS 16 treatment.

attributes.name: impairment_loss
attributes.description: Cumulative impairment loss recognised against the asset where the recoverable amount has fallen below the carrying amount. Recorded in accordance with IAS 36 and disclosed in financial statements.

attributes.name: insurance_policy_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the insurance policy covering the fixed asset. Used for insurance management, claims processing, and ensuring adequate coverage of high-value mining assets.

attributes.name: insured_value
attributes.description: Current insured replacement value of the asset as declared to the insurer. May differ from net book value; used for insurance adequacy reviews and risk management reporting.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the fixed asset master record in the source system. Used for change tracking, audit compliance, and incremental data loading.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; IFRS audit requirements

attributes.name: location_code
attributes.description: Specific physical location code within the plant or mine site where the asset is installed or stationed (e.g., processing circuit, pit bench, ROM pad). Corresponds to SAP ANLA-STORT.

attributes.name: lom_plan_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking the asset to the Life of Mine (LOM) plan under which it was approved and capitalised. Supports alignment of asset useful life with mine reserve depletion schedules for units-of-production depreciation.

attributes.name: net_book_value
attributes.description: Current net book value (NBV) of the asset, calculated as acquisition cost less accumulated depreciation and any impairment losses. Key balance sheet figure for CAPEX and financial disclosures.

attributes.name: purchase_order_number
attributes.description: SAP MM purchase order number associated with the acquisition of the asset. Provides the procurement audit trail linking the asset to the original purchase transaction.

attributes.name: remaining_useful_life_years
attributes.description: Remaining estimated useful life of the asset in years as at the current reporting date. Derived from useful life and elapsed depreciation periods; used for impairment assessments and LOM closure planning.

attributes.name: residual_value
attributes.description: Estimated residual or scrap value of the asset at the end of its useful life. Deducted from acquisition cost to determine the depreciable amount under IAS 16. Corresponds to SAP ANLC-SCHRW.

attributes.name: revaluation_amount
attributes.description: Cumulative revaluation surplus or deficit recognised for assets carried under the revaluation model per IAS 16. Applicable to mineral rights and land assets subject to periodic fair value assessment.

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer's serial number of the asset, used for warranty tracking, insurance purposes, and cross-referencing with the equipment maintenance register in Infor EAM.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the operational system of record from which this fixed asset record was sourced. Supports data lineage and reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and upstream systems.

attributes.name: useful_life_years
attributes.description: Estimated useful economic life of the asset in years as determined at the time of capitalisation or last review. Used for straight-line depreciation calculations and Life of Mine (LOM) planning alignment.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; IAS 16; LOM planning

attributes.name: vendor_code
attributes.description: SAP MM vendor code of the supplier from whom the asset was purchased. Used for warranty claims, procurement history, and vendor performance analysis.

attributes.name: reference_document_number

attributes.name: reversal_indicator

attributes.name: reversed_document_number

attributes.name: sending_company_code

attributes.name: settlement_date

attributes.name: settlement_status

attributes.name: site_code
attributes.description: Mining site or operation code associated with the intercompany transaction for operational tracking.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the source system from which the intercompany transaction data originated.

attributes.name: tax_jurisdiction_code
attributes.description: Tax jurisdiction code applicable to the intercompany transaction for withholding tax and compliance purposes.

attributes.name: transaction_amount

attributes.name: transaction_category

attributes.name: transaction_currency_code

attributes.name: transaction_document_number

products.name: hedge_instrument
products.description: Financial hedging instrument master capturing commodity price hedges (gold, copper, iron ore forwards and options), foreign currency contracts, and interest rate swaps used to manage mining revenue and cost exposure. Tracks instrument type, notional amount, strike/forward price, maturity date, counterparty, mark-to-market valuation, hedge effectiveness results, and IFRS 9 hedge accounting designation. Supports commodity revenue certainty, CAPEX FX protection, and treasury risk reporting.

attributes.name: hedge_instrument_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the financial hedging instrument record.

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: FK to finance.cost_centre

attributes.name: counterparty_id
attributes.description: FK to customer.counterparty

Business justification: Hedge instruments are posted to specific GL accounts for mark-to-market valuation (e.g., derivative asset/liability accounts, hedge reserve accounts). This link allows reconciling hedge instrument reg

attributes.name: profit_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_centre. Business justification: Hedging instruments should be allocated to profit centres for segment risk reporting. Commodity hedges are typically allocated to specific mine sites (profit centres) to match production exposure. Ess

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: FK to finance.wbs_element

attributes.name: aisc_inclusion_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether gains/losses from this hedging instrument are included in the calculation of All-In Sustaining Cost (AISC) for the mine site. True if included, False if excluded.

attributes.name: c1_cost_inclusion_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether gains/losses from this hedging instrument are included in the calculation of C1 Cash Cost for the mine site. True if included, False if excluded.

attributes.name: counterparty_credit_rating
attributes.description: The credit rating of the counterparty as assessed by a recognized rating agency (e.g., Moody's, S&P, Fitch), used for counterparty risk assessment.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this hedge instrument record was first created in the data system.

attributes.name: cumulative_gain_loss
attributes.description: The cumulative realized and unrealized gain or loss on the hedging instrument since inception, used for financial reporting and performance tracking.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which the hedging instrument becomes active and hedge accounting treatment begins, if designated.

attributes.name: hedge_accounting_designation
attributes.description: The IFRS 9 hedge accounting classification: fair value hedge (hedging changes in fair value of recognized asset/liability), cash flow hedge (hedging variability in future cash flows), net investment hedge (hedging FX risk in foreign operations), or not designated (held at fair value through profit or loss).

attributes.name: hedge_effectiveness_ratio_pct
attributes.description: The calculated hedge effectiveness ratio as a percentage, measuring the degree to which changes in the hedging instrument offset changes in the hedged item. IFRS 9 requires a ratio between 80% and 125% for hedge accounting qualification.

attributes.name: hedge_effectiveness_test_method
attributes.description: The method used to assess hedge effectiveness under IFRS 9 (e.g., dollar offset method, regression analysis, scenario analysis).

attributes.name: hedge_ratio
attributes.description: The ratio of the quantity of the hedging instrument to the quantity of the hedged item, used in hedge effectiveness calculations under IFRS 9.

attributes.name: hedged_item_description
attributes.description: Description of the underlying exposure or asset/liability being hedged (e.g., forecast copper sales Q1 2024, USD-denominated CAPEX for mine expansion, floating rate debt).

attributes.name: instrument_category
attributes.description: High-level categorization of the hedge by underlying risk exposure: commodity price hedge (gold, copper, iron ore), foreign currency hedge (FX protection for CAPEX or revenue), or interest rate hedge (debt cost management).

attributes.name: instrument_reference_number
attributes.description: External business identifier or contract number assigned to the hedging instrument by the treasury system or counterparty.

attributes.name: instrument_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the hedging instrument: active (open and in force), matured (reached maturity date), settled (closed out and settled), terminated (early termination by agreement), or cancelled (voided before execution).

attributes.name: instrument_type
attributes.description: Classification of the hedging instrument by derivative type: commodity forward, commodity option, foreign exchange (FX) forward, FX option, interest rate swap, or commodity swap.

attributes.name: last_effectiveness_test_date
attributes.description: The date on which the most recent hedge effectiveness test was performed.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this hedge instrument record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: mark_to_market_value
attributes.description: The current fair value or mark-to-market valuation of the hedging instrument, representing unrealized gain or loss at the reporting date.
attributes.references: IFRS 9 Financial Instruments, IFRS 13 Fair Value Measurement

attributes.name: maturity_date
attributes.description: The expiration or settlement date of the hedging instrument when the contract matures and is settled or exercised.

attributes.name: mtm_valuation_currency
attributes.description: The currency in which the mark-to-market value is reported (ISO 4217 three-letter code).

attributes.name: mtm_valuation_date
attributes.description: The date as of which the mark-to-market value was calculated or obtained.

attributes.name: notional_amount
attributes.description: The notional principal or contract size of the hedging instrument, representing the quantity or value being hedged (e.g., tonnes of copper, USD amount for FX forward).

attributes.name: notional_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the notional amount (e.g., tonnes, ounces, USD, AUD, barrels).

attributes.name: option_style
attributes.description: For option instruments, specifies the exercise style: European (exercisable only at maturity), American (exercisable any time before maturity), Asian (average price option), or not_applicable for non-option instruments.

attributes.name: option_type
attributes.description: For option instruments, specifies whether it is a call option (right to buy) or put option (right to sell). Set to not_applicable for forwards, swaps, and other non-option instruments.

attributes.name: premium_currency
attributes.description: The currency in which the option premium was paid (ISO 4217 three-letter code).

attributes.name: premium_paid
attributes.description: The upfront premium paid for option contracts. Null or zero for forward contracts and swaps that typically have no upfront premium.

attributes.name: sap_document_number
attributes.description: The SAP FI document number or treasury transaction reference linking this hedge instrument to the SAP S/4HANA financial system for audit trail and reconciliation.

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the hedging instrument was settled or closed out. Null if the instrument is still open.

attributes.name: strike_price
attributes.description: The agreed strike or exercise price for option contracts, or the forward price for forward contracts. Represents the price at which the hedge is executed.

attributes.name: strike_price_currency
attributes.description: The currency in which the strike or forward price is denominated (ISO 4217 three-letter code, e.g., USD, AUD, EUR).

attributes.name: trade_date
attributes.description: The date on which the hedging instrument was executed or contracted with the counterparty.

attributes.name: underlying_commodity
attributes.description: The specific commodity being hedged (gold, copper, iron ore, nickel, lithium, coal) for commodity price hedges. Set to not_applicable for FX and interest rate hedges. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: gold|copper|iron_ore|nickel|lithium|coal|not_applicable — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: underlying_currency_pair
attributes.description: The currency pair being hedged for foreign exchange instruments (e.g., USD/AUD, EUR/USD). Null for commodity and interest rate hedges.

products.name: cash_flow_forecast
products.description: Periodic cash flow forecast record capturing projected operating, investing, and financing cash flows by mine site, commodity, legal entity, and forecast horizon (weekly, monthly, quarterly, LOM). Tracks forecast inflows from commodity sales, hedging settlements, and asset disposals against outflows for CAPEX, OPEX, royalties, tax, debt service, and dividends. Includes forecast version, approval status, and variance to prior forecast. Supports treasury planning, debt covenant compliance monitoring, dividend capacity assessment, and board liquidity reporting for capital-intensive mining operations.

products.name: project_cost_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the cost allocation relationship between cost centres and capital projects in the mining portfolio. It captures the financial assignment of cost centre budgets and expenditure tracking to capital projects over specific time periods. Each record links one cost centre to one capital project with allocation percentages, budget amounts, cost categories, and effective date ranges that exist only in the context of this project-cost relationship. This enables accurate CAPEX tracking, project cost build-up, and multi-cost-centre project accounting.. Existence Justification: In mining operations, capital projects routinely span multiple cost centres (e.g., a shaft sinking project uses site services, engineering, construction, and equipment hire cost centres), and cost centres concurrently support multiple capital projects (e.g., the site engineering cost centre allocates effort across brownfield expansion, tailings raise, and sustaining capital projects). Finance teams actively manage these allocations with specific percentages, budget amounts, time periods, and cost categories to enable accurate CAPEX tracking and project cost build-up.

attributes.description: Approval status of the completed feasibility study by the investment committee or board: Pending Approval (submitted awaiting decision), Approved (endorsed for next stage), Rejected (not endorsed), Conditionally Approved (approved with conditions to be met), or Withdrawn (removed from consideration).

attributes.name: capital_cost_class
attributes.description: AACE International cost estimate classification: Class 5 (order of magnitude, -20% to -50% / +30% to +100%), Class 4 (study or feasibility, -15% to -30% / +20% to +50%), Class 3 (budget authorization or control, -10% to -20% / +10% to +30%), Class 2 (control or bid/tender, -5% to -15% / +5% to +20%), Class 1 (check estimate or bid/tender, -3% to -10% / +3% to +15%).

attributes.name: capital_cost_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the capital cost estimate (e.g., USD, AUD, CAD).

attributes.name: capital_cost_estimate
attributes.description: Total estimated capital expenditure required for the project as determined by the feasibility study, including mine development, plant construction, infrastructure, and pre-production costs.
attributes.references: AACE International Cost Estimate Classification System

attributes.name: commodity_price_assumption
attributes.description: Long-term commodity price assumption used in the economic evaluation of the feasibility study.

attributes.name: commodity_price_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the commodity price assumption (e.g., USD, AUD, CAD).

attributes.name: commodity_price_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the commodity price assumption: per tonne, per ounce, per pound, or per kilogram.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this feasibility study record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: discount_rate
attributes.description: Discount rate (as a percentage) used in the NPV and DCF calculations, typically representing the weighted average cost of capital (WACC) or hurdle rate.

attributes.name: environmental_approval_status
attributes.description: Status of environmental approvals and permits required for the project as assessed in the feasibility study: Not Required, Pending (not yet submitted), In Progress (under review by regulatory authorities), Approved (permits granted), or Rejected (permits denied).

attributes.name: exchange_rate_assumption
attributes.description: Foreign exchange rate assumption used in the economic evaluation, if the project operates in a currency different from the reporting currency.

attributes.name: irr
attributes.description: Internal rate of return calculated in the feasibility study, representing the discount rate at which the NPV of the project equals zero.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this feasibility study record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: lead_consultant
attributes.description: Name of the primary external consulting firm or engineering company responsible for conducting the feasibility study.

attributes.name: life_of_mine_years
attributes.description: Estimated life of mine in years as determined by the feasibility study, based on the ore reserve estimate and planned production rate.

attributes.name: npv
attributes.description: Net present value of the project calculated in the feasibility study, representing the present value of future cash flows discounted at the specified discount rate.

attributes.name: npv_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the NPV calculation (e.g., USD, AUD, CAD).

attributes.name: operating_cost_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the operating cost estimate (e.g., USD, AUD, CAD).

attributes.name: operating_cost_estimate
attributes.description: Estimated annual or life-of-mine average operating expenditure as determined by the feasibility study, including mining, processing, general and administrative costs.

attributes.name: operating_cost_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the operating cost estimate: per tonne ore processed, per tonne of product, per ounce of metal, per pound of metal, or per annum (annual total).
attributes.value_regex: per tonne ore|per tonne product|per ounce|per pound|per annum

attributes.name: payback_period_years
attributes.description: Estimated payback period in years, representing the time required to recover the initial capital investment from project cash flows.

attributes.name: production_rate_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the annual production rate: tonnes, ounces, pounds, or kilograms of the primary commodity.

attributes.name: risk_assessment_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether a comprehensive risk assessment was conducted as part of the feasibility study, covering technical, financial, environmental, social, and regulatory risks.

attributes.name: sensitivity_analysis_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether sensitivity analysis was performed to assess the impact of key variables (commodity price, operating costs, capital costs, exchange rates) on project economics.

attributes.name: social_impact_assessment_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether a social impact assessment was conducted to evaluate the projects effects on local communities, indigenous peoples, and other stakeholders.
attributes.references: ICMM Sustainable Development Framework, IFC Performance Standards

attributes.name: study_completion_date
attributes.description: Date when the feasibility study was completed and finalized for submission.

attributes.name: study_document_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or file path to the full feasibility study report document stored in the document management system.

attributes.name: study_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the feasibility study, typically including the project name and study type.

attributes.name: study_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the feasibility study, typically assigned by the project management office or engineering team.

attributes.name: study_scope
attributes.description: Detailed description of the scope of work covered by the feasibility study, including technical, economic, environmental, and social aspects evaluated.

attributes.name: study_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the feasibility study work officially commenced.

attributes.name: study_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the feasibility study: Planned (scheduled but not started), In Progress (actively being conducted), Under Review (submitted for internal or external review), Completed (finalized and approved), Cancelled (terminated before completion), or On Hold (temporarily suspended).

attributes.name: study_type
attributes.description: Classification of the study level: Scoping Study (conceptual), Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS - preliminary economic assessment), Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS - detailed engineering and economics), Bankable Feasibility Study (BFS - investment-grade), Trade-Off Study (comparison of alternatives), or Optimization Study (refinement of existing design).
attributes.value_regex: Scoping Study|Pre-Feasibility Study|Definitive Feasibility Study|Bankable Feasibility Study|Trade-Off Study|Optimization Study

attributes.name: superseded_feasibility_study_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on feasibility_study (superseded_feasibility_study_id)

products.name: phase
products.description: Defines the discrete execution phases of a capital project (Concept, Pre-Feasibility, Feasibility, FEED, Detailed Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Commissioning, Handover, Closeout). Captures phase name, planned start and finish dates, actual start and finish dates, phase budget allocation, phase status, and responsible project manager. Enables phase-level schedule and cost tracking within a project.

attributes.name: phase_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the project phase record. Primary key.

attributes.name: capital_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent capital project to which this phase belongs. Links phase to the overall project lifecycle.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee responsible for managing and delivering this specific phase. May differ from overall project manager for large multi-phase projects.

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Project phases align to WBS hierarchy for phase-gate cost tracking and capitalization decisions. Mining projects capitalize costs by phase (engineering, construction, commissioning) via WBS structure.

attributes.name: actual_cost
attributes.description: Total actual costs incurred to date for this phase, aggregated from all cost elements and work breakdown structure (WBS) elements within the phase.

attributes.name: actual_duration_days
attributes.description: Actual elapsed duration of the phase in calendar days from actual start to actual finish. Null if phase not yet completed.

attributes.name: actual_finish_date
attributes.description: Actual date when the phase was completed and formally closed. Null if phase is still in progress or not started.

attributes.name: actual_start_date
attributes.description: Actual date when work on the phase commenced. Null if phase has not yet started.

attributes.name: baseline_duration_days
attributes.description: Approved baseline duration for the phase in calendar days, calculated from planned start to planned finish.

attributes.name: budget_amount
attributes.description: Total approved budget allocated to this phase in the project's reporting currency. Represents the baseline cost for phase execution including Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) and Operating Expenditure (OPEX) components.

attributes.name: committed_cost
attributes.description: Total committed costs for this phase including purchase orders, contracts, and other financial commitments not yet invoiced.

attributes.name: completion_percentage
attributes.description: Current physical completion percentage of the phase based on earned value or milestone achievement. Value between 0.00 and 100.00.

attributes.name: cost_variance_amount
attributes.description: Current cost variance calculated as phase budget minus phase forecast cost. Negative values indicate cost overrun.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this phase record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage.

attributes.name: critical_path_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this phase is on the project's critical path. True if any delay in this phase will delay overall project completion.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this phase record (e.g., USD, AUD, CAD, ZAR).

attributes.name: forecast_cost
attributes.description: Current forecast of total cost at completion for this phase, updated regularly based on actuals, commitments, and estimates to complete.

attributes.name: forecast_finish_date
attributes.description: Current best estimate of when the phase will complete, updated regularly based on progress and risks. Used for schedule variance analysis.

attributes.name: gate_approval_authority
attributes.description: Name or title of the governance body or individual who granted stage-gate approval (e.g., Executive Committee, Board of Directors, Capital Allocation Committee).

attributes.name: gate_approval_date
attributes.description: Date when formal stage-gate approval was granted for this phase to proceed. Null if approval not yet obtained or not required.

attributes.name: gate_approval_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether formal stage-gate approval is required before this phase can commence. True if governance approval is mandatory.

attributes.name: key_deliverables
attributes.description: Summary list of major deliverables and outputs expected from this phase (e.g., feasibility study report, detailed engineering drawings, procurement contracts, construction completion certificate).

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, issues, decisions, or commentary related to phase execution and performance.

attributes.name: phase_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the phase type within the organization's project methodology (e.g., CONCEPT, PREFEAS, FEAS, FEED, DETAIL_ENG, PROCURE, CONSTRUCT, COMMISSION, HANDOVER, CLOSEOUT).

attributes.name: phase_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the phase scope, objectives, key deliverables, and success criteria. Provides context for phase execution and governance.

attributes.name: phase_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the project phase (e.g., Concept Study, Pre-Feasibility Study, Feasibility Study, Front-End Engineering Design, Detailed Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Commissioning, Handover, Project Closeout).

attributes.name: phase_status
attributes.description: Current execution status of the project phase indicating its lifecycle state.

attributes.name: planned_finish_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date when the phase is planned to complete according to the baseline project schedule.

attributes.name: planned_start_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date when the phase is planned to commence according to the baseline project schedule.

attributes.name: record_active_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this phase record is currently active and valid. False if the record has been logically deleted or superseded.

attributes.name: risk_rating
attributes.description: Overall risk assessment for this phase based on schedule, cost, technical, and external risk factors. Used for prioritizing management attention.

attributes.name: schedule_variance_days
attributes.description: Current schedule variance in calendar days, calculated as the difference between forecast finish and planned finish. Negative values indicate delay.

attributes.name: sequence
attributes.description: Ordinal position of this phase within the project's overall phase sequence. Used to enforce phase ordering and dependencies.

attributes.name: updated_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last updated this phase record. Supports audit and accountability.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this phase record was last modified. Audit trail for change tracking.

attributes.name: predecessor_phase_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on phase (predecessor_phase_id)

products.name: schedule
products.description: Master record of the project schedule baseline and current schedule for a capital project or phase. Captures schedule version, baseline approval date, total float, critical path flag, schedule performance index (SPI), planned completion date, forecast completion date, schedule variance in days, and the scheduling tool reference (Primavera P6, MS Project). Serves as the SSOT for schedule status and earned value schedule metrics.

attributes.name: schedule_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the project schedule record. Primary key.

attributes.name: capital_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the capital project or phase that this schedule belongs to. Links to the parent project entity.

attributes.name: actual_completion_date
attributes.description: Actual date when the project or phase was completed and handed over. Populated upon project closure.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the project manager, project director, or governance authority who approved this schedule version. Critical for baseline control and change management.

attributes.name: baseline_approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the schedule baseline was formally approved by the project governance board or steering committee. Critical for earned value management and schedule variance analysis.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Earned Value Management

attributes.name: completed_activities_count
attributes.description: Number of activities that have been completed as of the schedule status date. Used to calculate percent complete and progress metrics.

attributes.name: compression_method
attributes.description: Method applied to compress the schedule and reduce project duration. Fast tracking involves overlapping activities that were originally sequential. Crashing involves adding resources to critical path activities. Both may be applied simultaneously.

attributes.name: contingency_days
attributes.description: Time buffer or contingency reserve built into the schedule to account for schedule risks and uncertainties. Managed as part of schedule risk management.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this schedule record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: critical_activities_count
attributes.description: Number of activities on the critical path. Used to assess schedule risk concentration and management focus areas.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: critical_path_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this schedule version identifies activities on the critical path. True if critical path analysis has been performed and critical activities are flagged in the detailed schedule.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: data_date
attributes.description: Status date or as-of date for the schedule. Represents the point in time up to which actual progress has been recorded and from which forecasts are projected. Critical reference point for earned value calculations.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Earned Value Management

attributes.name: forecast_completion_date
attributes.description: Current projected completion date based on actual progress, remaining work, and schedule performance trends. Updated regularly as part of schedule control processes.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Earned Value Management

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this schedule record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: last_update_date
attributes.description: Date when the schedule was last updated with actual progress and forecast changes. Used to assess schedule data currency.

attributes.name: longest_path_duration_days
attributes.description: Duration in days of the longest path through the schedule network from start to finish. Represents the minimum project duration assuming no resource constraints.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes and comments about the schedule version, including assumptions, constraints, key changes from previous versions, and schedule management decisions.

attributes.name: percent_complete
attributes.description: Overall schedule completion percentage based on completed activities or earned value. Expressed as a value between 0 and 100.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Earned Value Management

attributes.name: performance_index
attributes.description: Earned value schedule performance index calculated as Earned Value (EV) divided by Planned Value (PV). Values less than 1.0 indicate schedule delays, values greater than 1.0 indicate schedule advancement. Key earned value metric for project control.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Earned Value Management

attributes.name: performance_index_date
attributes.description: Date as of which the schedule performance index was calculated. Important for tracking SPI trends over time.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Earned Value Management

attributes.name: planned_completion_date
attributes.description: Original baseline completion date for the project as per the approved schedule. Used as the reference point for schedule variance calculations.

attributes.name: prepared_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the project scheduler or planning engineer who prepared this schedule version. Used for accountability and schedule quality assurance.

attributes.name: risk_level
attributes.description: Overall assessment of schedule risk based on float consumption, critical path stability, resource constraints, and external dependencies. Used for escalation and management attention.

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the schedule. Tracks the approval and activation state of the schedule version.

attributes.name: schedule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the schedule record. Baseline represents the approved reference schedule, current is the working schedule, forecast is the projected schedule, what-if is scenario planning, and recovery is a corrective action schedule.

attributes.name: scheduling_tool
attributes.description: Software application used to create and maintain the project schedule. Common tools in mining include Primavera P6 for large capital projects, MS Project for smaller projects, and Deswik or Minex for mine-specific scheduling.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Schedule Management Tools

attributes.name: scheduling_tool_file_reference
attributes.description: File path, document management system reference, or unique identifier for the native schedule file in the scheduling tool. Enables traceability to the source schedule data.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual start date of the project schedule. Represents the earliest activity start in the schedule network.

attributes.name: total_activities_count
attributes.description: Total number of activities or tasks in the project schedule. Provides a measure of schedule complexity and granularity.

attributes.name: total_float_days
attributes.description: Total float or slack available in the schedule network. Represents the amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the project completion date. Critical for risk management and resource optimization.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: update_frequency
attributes.description: Planned frequency for updating the project schedule with actual progress and forecast changes. Typically defined in the project management plan.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Schedule Management Plan

attributes.name: variance_days
attributes.description: Difference in days between the planned completion date and the forecast completion date. Negative values indicate schedule delay, positive values indicate schedule advancement. Key metric for schedule performance monitoring.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Earned Value Management

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version identifier for the schedule baseline or update. Used to track schedule revisions over the project lifecycle.

attributes.name: superseded_schedule_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on schedule (superseded_schedule_id)

products.name: schedule_activity
products.description: Individual schedule activity (task) within a project schedule, derived from the Primavera P6 WBS. Captures activity ID, activity name, WBS code, activity type (Level of Effort, Milestone, Task Dependent), planned start, planned finish, actual start, actual finish, original duration, remaining duration, percent complete, total float, free float, and critical path flag. Enables granular schedule tracking and critical path analysis.

attributes.name: schedule_activity_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the schedule activity within the project schedule. Primary key.

attributes.name: calendar_id
attributes.description: Reference to the work calendar applied to this activity, defining working days, shifts, and holidays used for duration calculations.

attributes.name: capital_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent project to which this schedule activity belongs.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Project Integration Management

attributes.name: phase_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to project.phase. Business justification: Individual schedule activities occur within specific project phases. Currently schedule_activity links to capital_project and wbs_element but not directly to phase. This enables phase-level schedule r

attributes.name: primary_schedule_wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Reference to the WBS element under which this activity is organized.

attributes.name: schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to project.project_schedule. Business justification: Schedule activities belong to a project schedule (baseline, current, forecast). Currently schedule_activity has project_id but no FK to project_schedule. This is a critical parent-child relationship -

attributes.name: activity_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the schedule activity, typically sourced from Primavera P6 or similar scheduling system.

attributes.name: activity_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the schedule activity, clearly identifying the work to be performed.

attributes.name: activity_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes and comments related to the activity, capturing progress updates, issues, decisions, or other relevant information.

attributes.name: activity_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the schedule activity indicating progress state.

attributes.name: activity_type
attributes.description: Classification of the activity type indicating how it is scheduled and tracked. Task Dependent activities have duration and dependencies; Milestones mark key events with zero duration; Level of Effort activities span a time period without discrete deliverables; WBS Summary activities aggregate subordinate tasks.

attributes.name: actual_cost
attributes.description: The actual cost incurred for this activity to date, used for cost performance analysis and variance reporting.

attributes.name: actual_duration_days
attributes.description: The actual number of working days taken to complete the activity, calculated from actual start to actual finish dates.

attributes.name: actual_finish_date
attributes.description: The actual date when work on this activity was completed. Null if activity is not yet finished.

attributes.name: actual_labour_hours
attributes.description: The actual labour hours expended on this activity to date, used for productivity analysis and resource performance tracking.

attributes.name: actual_start_date
attributes.description: The actual date when work on this activity commenced. Null if activity has not yet started.

attributes.name: budgeted_cost
attributes.description: The total budgeted cost allocated to this activity, representing the planned value for earned value management calculations.

attributes.name: budgeted_labour_hours
attributes.description: The total planned labour hours allocated to this activity across all resources.

attributes.name: constraint_date
attributes.description: The date associated with the constraint type, defining the earliest, latest, or mandatory date for activity start or finish.

attributes.name: constraint_type
attributes.description: Type of schedule constraint applied to this activity, restricting when it can be scheduled relative to a constraint date. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: as_soon_as_possible|as_late_as_possible|start_no_earlier_than|start_no_later_than|finish_no_earlier_than|finish_no_later_than|must_start_on|must_finish_on — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this schedule activity record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: data_date
attributes.description: The status date or as-of date for which the schedule data was current, representing the point in time when progress was last updated.

attributes.name: discipline_code
attributes.description: Code representing the engineering or operational discipline associated with this activity (e.g., civil, mechanical, electrical, mining, processing).

attributes.name: early_finish_date
attributes.description: The earliest possible date the activity can finish based on network logic and predecessor constraints, calculated via Critical Path Method (CPM).
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: early_start_date
attributes.description: The earliest possible date the activity can start based on network logic and predecessor constraints, calculated via Critical Path Method (CPM).
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: free_float_days
attributes.description: The amount of time in working days that the activity can be delayed without delaying the early start of any successor activity.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: is_critical_path
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this activity is on the critical path (True) or not (False). Critical path activities have zero or negative total float and directly impact project completion date.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this schedule activity record was most recently modified.

attributes.name: late_finish_date
attributes.description: The latest date the activity can finish without delaying the project finish date, calculated via Critical Path Method (CPM).
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: late_start_date
attributes.description: The latest date the activity can start without delaying the project finish date, calculated via Critical Path Method (CPM).
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: original_duration_days
attributes.description: The initially estimated duration of the activity in working days as defined in the baseline schedule.

attributes.name: percent_complete
attributes.description: The percentage of work completed for this activity, expressed as a value between 0.00 and 100.00, used for progress tracking and earned value calculations.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Earned Value Management

attributes.name: planned_finish_date
attributes.description: The originally planned or baseline finish date for the activity as per the approved project schedule.

attributes.name: planned_start_date
attributes.description: The originally planned or baseline start date for the activity as per the approved project schedule.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Numeric priority ranking for the activity, used for resource leveling and conflict resolution. Lower numbers typically indicate higher priority.

attributes.name: remaining_duration_days
attributes.description: The estimated number of working days required to complete the activity from the data date, updated during schedule progress updates.

attributes.name: responsible_party
attributes.description: The organization, contractor, or functional group responsible for executing this activity.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The name of the source system from which this schedule activity data originated (e.g., Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, SAP PS).

attributes.name: total_float_days
attributes.description: The amount of time in working days that the activity can be delayed without delaying the project finish date. Calculated as Late Start minus Early Start (or Late Finish minus Early Finish).
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: predecessor_schedule_activity_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on schedule_activity (predecessor_schedule_activity_id)

products.name: milestone
products.description: Key project milestone record representing a significant deliverable or decision point within a capital project. Captures milestone name, milestone type (contractual, internal, regulatory, financial), planned date, forecast date, actual achieved date, milestone status (Not Started, At Risk, Achieved, Missed), responsible party, and any delay reason code. Used for executive reporting, contractor performance, and stage-gate readiness tracking.

attributes.name: milestone_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the project milestone record. Primary key.

attributes.name: capital_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent capital project to which this milestone belongs. Links milestone to the overarching mine development, plant expansion, or infrastructure project.

attributes.name: phase_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to project.phase. Business justification: Milestones occur within specific project phases. Currently milestone links to capital_project but not to the specific phase, missing a hierarchical relationship. This enables phase-level milestone tra

attributes.name: predecessor_milestone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the milestone that must be completed before this milestone can begin or be achieved. Used for schedule dependency tracking and critical path analysis.

attributes.name: procurement_purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: Project milestones tied to PO delivery (long-lead equipment arrival gates). Business process: critical path management, schedule risk tracking, milestone payment triggers linked to procurement.

attributes.name: accountable_person
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the individual who is ultimately accountable for milestone achievement. Typically a project manager, engineering lead, or contractor representative.

attributes.name: actual_date
attributes.description: The actual date when the milestone was achieved and acceptance criteria were met. Populated only after milestone completion and formal sign-off.

attributes.name: approval_authority
attributes.description: The governance body, executive role, or regulatory authority that must formally approve or sign off on this milestone achievement. Examples include Project Steering Committee, CEO, Board of Directors, or regulatory agency.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date when the milestone achievement was formally approved or signed off by the designated approval authority. May differ from actual achievement date if approval process takes time.

attributes.name: baseline_date
attributes.description: The approved baseline date for the milestone after any formal re-baselining or change control approvals. Used for performance measurement when the original plan has been formally revised.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, observations, or context about the milestone status, progress, issues, or achievements. Used for qualitative reporting and knowledge capture.

attributes.name: contractual_obligation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this milestone is a contractual obligation with financial or legal consequences. True means the milestone is tied to contract terms, payment schedules, or liquidated damages provisions.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this milestone record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: criticality_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this milestone is on the critical path of the project schedule. True means any delay to this milestone will directly impact the overall project completion date.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the milestone payment amount (e.g., USD, AUD, CAD). Used for multi-currency project tracking and financial reporting.

attributes.name: delay_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code representing the primary reason for milestone delay or at-risk status. Used for root cause analysis and trend reporting across projects. Examples include weather, equipment delivery, design changes, regulatory approval delays, labor shortages.

attributes.name: delay_reason_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative explanation of the delay reason, including specific circumstances, contributing factors, and any mitigation actions taken or planned.

attributes.name: evidence_document_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or location of the supporting documentation that provides evidence of milestone completion. May include test reports, inspection certificates, regulatory approvals, or sign-off documents.

attributes.name: forecast_date
attributes.description: The current projected date when the milestone is expected to be achieved, based on actual progress and updated schedule analysis. Updated regularly during project execution.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this milestone record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking and data currency verification.

attributes.name: milestone_category
attributes.description: The project phase or functional category to which the milestone belongs. Used for grouping milestones by lifecycle stage for reporting and tracking purposes.

attributes.name: milestone_code
attributes.description: Business identifier or code for the milestone, often used in project schedules and contractor agreements. May follow organizational or project-specific coding conventions.

attributes.name: milestone_description

products.name: change_order
products.description: Formal project change order record capturing approved scope, schedule, or cost changes to a capital project. Feeds budget amendments and schedule updates.

attributes.name: change_order_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the project change order record. Primary key for the change order entity.

attributes.name: capital_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the capital project to which this change order applies. Links the change order to the parent project record.

attributes.name: procurement_purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: Project change orders trigger PO amendments for scope changes. Business process: procurement impact assessment, cost change tracking, PO modification workflow, change order cost validation.

attributes.name: project_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to project.project_contract. Business justification: Change orders are often raised against project contracts (contract variations). Currently change_order has contract_reference (STRING) and contractor_name (STRING). Adding project_contract_id FK creat

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Change orders impact WBS budget baselines and require budget amendment approvals. Mining projects track scope changes against WBS for cost variance analysis and audit trails.

attributes.name: approval_authority_level
attributes.description: Hierarchical level of approval authority required for this change order, typically determined by the magnitude of cost and schedule impact. Ensures appropriate governance oversight.
attributes.value_regex: Project Manager|Project Director|Change Control Board|Executive Steering Committee|Board of Directors

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the change order was formally approved by the designated approving authority. Null if the change order is pending, rejected, or withdrawn.

attributes.name: approving_authority
attributes.description: Name or title of the individual or governance body authorized to approve or reject the change order (e.g., Project Manager, Project Director, Change Control Board, Steering Committee). Reflects delegation of authority based on change order value and impact.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Change Control Board

attributes.name: baseline_update_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the approved change order has been incorporated into the project baseline (scope, schedule, cost). True indicates baseline has been updated; False indicates pending baseline update.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Integrated Change Control

attributes.name: capex_impact_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the cost impact that affects capital expenditure budget. Used for tracking changes to capitalized project costs and asset valuation.
attributes.references: IFRS - IAS 16 Property Plant and Equipment

attributes.name: change_category
attributes.description: Functional area or discipline impacted by the change order. Identifies which project domain (engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, health safety environment, regulatory, commercial, or schedule) is primarily affected. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Engineering|Procurement|Construction|Commissioning|HSE|Regulatory|Commercial|Schedule — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: change_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the proposed change, including technical specifications, scope modifications, rationale, and business justification. Provides comprehensive context for approval decision-making.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Change Request Documentation

attributes.name: change_justification
attributes.description: Business rationale and justification for the change order. Explains why the change is necessary, the risks of not implementing it, and the expected benefits or risk mitigation achieved.

attributes.name: change_order_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the change order, typically following organizational numbering convention (e.g., CO-000123). Used for communication, approvals, and audit trails.

attributes.name: change_order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the change order in the approval and implementation workflow. Tracks progression from initial draft through approval to implementation and closure. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Draft|Submitted|Under Review|Approved|Rejected|Withdrawn|Implemented|Closed — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Change Control Process

attributes.name: change_title
attributes.description: Brief descriptive title summarizing the change order for quick identification and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: change_type
attributes.description: Classification of the nature of the change request. Categorizes whether the change adds scope, reduces scope, modifies design, addresses regulatory requirements, responds to force majeure events, or adjusts schedule without scope impact.
attributes.value_regex: Scope Addition|Scope Reduction|Design Change|Regulatory Requirement|Force Majeure|Schedule Adjustment

attributes.name: cost_impact_amount
attributes.description: Total financial impact of the change order on the project budget, expressed in the project currency. Positive values indicate cost increases; negative values indicate cost savings. Used for budget amendment and cost control reporting.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the change order record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and tracking change order lifecycle duration.

attributes.name: critical_path_impact_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the change order impacts activities on the project critical path. True indicates the change affects critical path and may delay project completion; False indicates non-critical path impact.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Critical Path Method

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the cost impact amount (e.g., USD, AUD, CAD). Ensures consistent financial reporting across multi-currency projects.

attributes.name: hse_impact_assessment
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Safety and Environment (HSE) Impact Assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of how the change order affects health, safety, and environmental aspects of the project. Identifies new HSE risks, mitigation measures, or improvements to HSE performance.
attributes.references: ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety, ISO 14001 Environmental Management

attributes.name: implementation_date
attributes.description: Date when the approved change order was implemented and incorporated into the project baseline (scope, schedule, budget). Used for tracking change order execution and project baseline updates.
attributes.references: PMI PMBOK Guide - Integrated Change Control

attributes.name: milestone_impact_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of how the change order affects key project milestones, including which milestones are impacted and the nature of the impact (delay, acceleration, scope change).

attributes.name: opex_impact_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the cost impact that affects operating expenditure budget. Used for tracking changes to operational costs during commissioning or early operations phases.
attributes.references: IFRS - IAS 1 Presentation of Financial Statements

attributes.name: originator_name
attributes.description: Name of the individual or party who initiated the change order request. May be internal project team member, contractor, consultant, or regulatory authority.

attributes.name: originator_organization
attributes.description: Organization or company that the change order originator represents (e.g., owner, contractor, subcontractor, engineering firm, regulatory body).

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Priority level assigned to the change order for review and approval processing. Critical and High priority changes require expedited review due to schedule or safety impacts.

attributes.name: quality_impact_assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of how the change order affects project quality standards, specifications, or deliverable quality. Identifies any quality improvements or potential quality risks.

attributes.name: rejection_date
attributes.description: Date when the change order was formally rejected by the approving authority. Null if not rejected.

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Explanation provided by the approving authority for rejecting the change order. Null if the change order was not rejected. Used for lessons learned and continuous improvement.

attributes.name: required_by_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the change order decision is required to avoid project delays or other negative impacts. Used for prioritizing review and approval activities.

attributes.name: review_comments
attributes.description: Comments and feedback provided by reviewers during the change order evaluation process. Captures discussion points, concerns raised, and conditions for approval.

attributes.name: risk_impact_assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of how the change order affects project risks, including new risks introduced, existing risks mitigated, or changes to risk exposure. Supports risk-informed decision-making.

attributes.name: schedule_impact_days
attributes.description: Impact of the change order on the project schedule, measured in calendar days. Positive values indicate schedule delays; negative values indicate schedule acceleration. Used for schedule baseline updates and critical path analysis.

attributes.name: scope_impact_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of how the change order modifies the project scope, including additions, deletions, or modifications to deliverables, specifications, or work breakdown structure elements.

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Date when the change order was formally submitted for review and approval. Marks the start of the approval workflow and is used for tracking approval cycle time.

attributes.name: supporting_documents
attributes.description: References or file paths to supporting documentation for the change order, such as technical drawings, cost estimates, schedule impact analysis, risk assessments, or regulatory correspondence.

attributes.name: updated_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last modified the change order record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the change order record was last modified. Used for audit trail and tracking change order progression through workflow stages.

attributes.name: withdrawal_reason
attributes.description: Explanation provided by the originator for withdrawing the change order before approval decision. Null if the change order was not withdrawn.

attributes.name: superseded_change_order_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on change_order (superseded_change_order_id)

attributes.name: key_assumptions

attributes.name: last_review_date

attributes.name: monte_carlo_iterations

attributes.name: next_review_date

attributes.description: Code identifying the project phase to which this risk register applies (e.g., FEASIBILITY, DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, COMMISSIONING).

attributes.name: record_active_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this risk register record is currently active (True) or has been logically deleted or archived (False).

attributes.name: register_code
attributes.description: Business identifier or code for the risk register, typically following organizational naming conventions (e.g., RR-PROJECT-001).

attributes.name: register_date
attributes.description: The effective date of this risk register version, representing the baseline date for the risk assessment snapshot.

attributes.name: register_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the risk register purpose, scope, and context within the project lifecycle.

attributes.name: register_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the risk register, typically including the project name and version or phase identifier.

attributes.name: register_notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or context relevant to this risk register version, including changes from previous versions.

attributes.name: register_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the risk register indicating its approval state and usability for decision-making.

attributes.name: register_version
attributes.description: Version number or identifier of the risk register, incremented with each major update or review cycle.

attributes.name: risk_appetite_statement
attributes.description: Statement describing the organizations risk appetite and tolerance levels applicable to this project and risk register.

attributes.name: risk_framework
attributes.description: The risk management framework or standard applied (e.g., ISO 31000, COSO ERM, PMI Risk Management).

attributes.name: risk_methodology

attributes.name: risk_threshold_cost_usd
